title.zh: 卷四百二十一 列傳第一百八十 楊棟 姚希得 包恢 常挺 陳宗禮 常楙 家鉉翁 李庭芝
title.en: Volume 421 Biographies 180: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, Li Tingzhi
title.raw: 卷四百二十一 列傳第一百八十 楊棟 姚希得 包恢 常挺 陳宗禮 常楙 家鉉翁 李庭芝 Volume 421 Biographies 180: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, Li Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 楊棟 姚希得 包恢 常挺 陳宗禮 常楙 家鉉翁 李庭芝

translations.literal: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, Li Tingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, and Li Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 楊棟，字元極，眉州青城人。

translations.literal: Yang Dong, style name Yuanji, was a man of Qingcheng in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dong, whose style was Yuanji, came from Qingcheng in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年進士第二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding he was second among jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Shaoding reign he placed second on the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授簽書劍南西川節度判官廳公事。

translations.literal: He was appointed signing clerk for the administrative office of the Jiannan West Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed signing clerk in the administrative office of the Jiannan West Circuit military commission.

sentences.zh: 未上，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, his mother died and he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，遷荊南制置司，改辟西川，入為太學正。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to the Jingnan military commission, then reassigned by invitation to the West Circuit commission, and entered the capital as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was posted to the Jingnan military commission, then transferred by invitation to the West Circuit commission, and finally entered the capital as director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，召試授秘書省正字兼吳益王府教授，遷校書郎、樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: His father died; when mourning ended he was summoned for examination and appointed rectifier of the Secretariat concurrently instructor at the Prince of Wu Yi estate; he was promoted to collating editor and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died and mourning ended, he was summoned for examination and appointed rectifier of the Secretariat while also serving as instructor at the Prince of Wu Yi’s household; he was then promoted to collating editor and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「飛蝗蔽天，願陛下始終一德，庶幾感格天心，消弭災咎。」

translations.literal: At audience he said: 'Flying locusts cover the sky. I hope Your Majesty will keep one virtue from beginning to end, so that perhaps Heaven’s heart may be moved and disasters quelled.'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he said, “Locusts blot out the sky. I beg Your Majesty to hold fast to a single consistent virtue from first to last, so that Heaven’s heart may be touched and these calamities put to rest.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「邇來中外之臣，如主兵理財，聽其言無非可用，跡其實類皆欺誣，上下相蒙，無一可信。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Recently ministers inside and outside court—whether in charge of troops or finances—hear their words and none seem unusable; trace their deeds and they mostly deceive. Above and below deceive one another; not one can be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “Of late, whether at court or in the provinces, those who command armies or manage finances—listen to what they say and it all sounds workable; look at what they actually do and it is mostly deceit. Court and country deceive one another; there is no one left to trust.

sentences.zh: 陛下先之以至誠，而後天下之事可為也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty must take the lead with utmost sincerity; only then can affairs under Heaven be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty leads with utmost sincerity can anything under Heaven truly be accomplished.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「祖宗立國，不恃兵財法，惟恃民心固結而已。

translations.literal: He also said: 'When our ancestors founded the state they did not rely on armies, wealth, or law, but solely on binding the people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “When our founders established the dynasty they did not rely on armies, wealth, or statutes, but solely on binding the people’s hearts together.

sentences.zh: 願陛下常存忠厚之意，勿用峻急之人。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will always keep a generous and honest intent and not employ harsh and precipitate men.'
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will always keep a generous and honest disposition, and will not put harsh and precipitate men in power.”

sentences.zh: 理宗悅，以臣僚言奉祠。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong was pleased; on a colleague’s motion he was granted a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong was pleased; on a colleague’s recommendation he was granted a ceremonial post.

sentences.zh: 起知興化軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as military prefect of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 孔子之裔有居𣷉頭鎮者，棟為建廟辟田，訓其子弟。

translations.literal: Descendants of Confucius lived at Paitou town; Dong built a temple for them, set aside fields, and instructed their sons and younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Confucius who lived at Paitou town—Dong built a temple for them, set aside fields, and taught their young.

sentences.zh: 遷福建提點刑獄，尋加直秘閣兼權知福州，兼本路安撫使，遷都官郎官，又遷左司郎官，尋為右司郎官兼玉牒所檢討官，除宗正少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fujian judicial intendant, soon given direct appointment to the Secretariat and concurrent acting prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of that circuit; promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Left Division director; soon Right Division director concurrently examiner at the Imperial Genealogy Office; appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Fujian judicial intendant, soon given direct appointment to the Secretariat while also serving as acting prefect of Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of that circuit; he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then to Left Division director, and soon became Right Division director while also serving as examiner at the Imperial Genealogy Office; he was appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 進對，帝曰：「止是正心修身之說乎？」

translations.literal: At audience the Emperor said: 'Is it only the doctrine of rectifying the mind and cultivating the person?'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience the Emperor said, “Is that all—just the teaching about rectifying the mind and cultivating the person?”

sentences.zh: 棟對曰：「臣所學三十年，止此一說。

translations.literal: Dong replied: 'What this subject has studied for thirty years is solely this one doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Dong replied, “What I have studied for thirty years is this one teaching alone.

sentences.zh: 用之事親取友，用之治雕郡、察冤獄，至為簡易。」

translations.literal: Apply it to serving parents and choosing friends; apply it to governing carved-out prefectures and examining wrongful cases—it is still the same and simple.'
translations.idiomatic: Apply it to honoring parents and choosing friends, apply it to governing a remote prefecture or examining wrongful cases—it is still the same, and still simple.”

sentences.zh: 時有女冠出入宮禁，頗通請謁，外廷多有以為言者。

translations.literal: At the time a female Daoist priest went in and out of the palace forbidden quarter, conducted favor-seeking rather freely, and many at the outer court spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a female Daoist priest was going in and out of the inner palace, openly trading on petitions and favors, and many at the outer court were speaking of it.

sentences.zh: 棟上疏曰：「陛下何惜一女冠，天下所側目而不亟去之乎？」

translations.literal: Dong memorialized: 'Your Majesty, why spare one female Daoist priest when all under Heaven watch askance and you do not remove her promptly?'
translations.idiomatic: Dong submitted a memorial: “Your Majesty, why spare a single female Daoist when the whole realm watches in dismay and you do not remove her at once?”

sentences.zh: 帝不謂然。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 棟曰：「此人密交小人，甚可慮也。」

translations.literal: Dong said: 'This person secretly associates with petty men; she is greatly to be feared.'
translations.idiomatic: Dong said, “This person secretly consorts with petty men; she is deeply alarming.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「京、襄、兩淮、四川殘破郡縣之吏，多是兵將權攝，科取無藝，其民可矜，非陛下哀之，誰實哀之。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'In ruined prefectures and counties of Jing, Xiang, the two Huai circuits, and Sichuan, many officials are military men exercising temporary authority, extracting levies without limit; those people deserve pity—if Your Majesty does not pity them, who truly will?'
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “In the shattered prefectures and counties of Jing, Xiang, the two Huai circuits, and Sichuan, most officials are military men holding temporary authority, levying exactions without restraint. Those people deserve pity—if Your Majesty does not pity them, who truly will?”

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿、起居郎，差知滁州，以殿中侍御史周坦論罷。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and drafter of the Privy Archives, assigned prefect of Chuzhou, and removed on impeachment by Censor Zhou Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and drafter of the Privy Archives, then assigned as prefect of Chuzhou, but was dismissed after impeachment by the palace censor Zhou Tan.

sentences.zh: 起直龍圖閣、知建寧府，不拜。

translations.literal: He was recalled with direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall and as prefect of Jianning, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled with direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall and as prefect of Jianning, but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 提舉千秋鴻禧觀，遷起居郎兼權侍左侍郎、崇政殿說書，繼遷吏部侍郎兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼侍讀，以集英殿修撰兼中書舍人兼侍講，出知太平州，以右補闕蕭泰來論罷，依舊職提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was made superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey, promoted drafter of the Privy Archives concurrently acting vice minister of the left secretariat and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, then vice minister of Personnel concurrently co-compiler of the National History and co-author of the Veritable Records while also reader-in-waiting; as compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence he was also drafting secretary and lecturer-in-waiting, then sent out as prefect of Taiping, removed on impeachment by Remonstrance Officer Xiao Tailai, and made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey, promoted to drafter of the Privy Archives while also serving as acting vice minister of the left secretariat and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, then to vice minister of Personnel while also co-compiling the National History and the Veritable Records and serving as reader-in-waiting; as compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence he also served as drafting secretary and lecturer-in-waiting, then was sent out as prefect of Taiping, dismissed after impeachment by the remonstrance officer Xiao Tailai, and appointed superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 起知婺州。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召奏事，以舊職奉祠。

translations.literal: Summoned to report on affairs, he was granted a sinecure at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to report on affairs, he was granted a ceremonial post at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 度宗立為太子，帝親擢棟太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong was established as heir apparent, the Emperor personally promoted Dong to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong was installed as heir apparent, the Emperor personally promoted Dong to tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，仍為詹事兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼中書舍人，兼直學士院，權刑部尚書兼國子祭酒，遷禮部尚書，加端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事兼太子賓客，進同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice minister of Works while remaining tutor, concurrently co-compiler of the National History and co-author of the Veritable Records and drafting secretary, also academician of the Hanlin Academy, acting minister of Justice and chancellor of the Imperial University, then minister of Rites; given academician of the Duanming Hall, co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the heir apparent, advanced to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, and appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works while remaining tutor of the crown prince, also co-compiling the National History and Veritable Records and serving as drafting secretary, then as academician of the Hanlin Academy, acting minister of Justice and chancellor of the Imperial University, and finally minister of Rites; he was given the title academician of the Duanming Hall, made co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the crown prince, advanced to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 臺州守王華甫建上蔡書院，言於朝，乞棟為山主，詔從之。

translations.literal: Taizhou prefect Wang Huafu built the Shangcai Academy, spoke of it at court, and requested Dong as its head; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huafu, prefect of Taizhou, founded the Shangcai Academy, petitioned the court to appoint Dong as its head, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 因卜居於臺。

translations.literal: He therefore chose residence at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly made his home in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授資政殿學士、知建寧府，不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was given academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Jianning, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Jianning, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 以舊職提舉洞霄宮，復依舊職知慶元府、沿海制置使。

translations.literal: At his former rank he was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey, then again at his former rank prefect of Qingyuan and coastal military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At his former rank he was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey, then again appointed prefect of Qingyuan and coastal military commissioner at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史胡用虎言罷，仍奉祠。

translations.literal: He was removed on the words of investigating censor Hu Yonghu and again granted a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after impeachment by the investigating censor Hu Yonghu and again granted a ceremonial post.

sentences.zh: 加觀文殿學士知慶元府、沿海制置使，又不拜，仍奉祠。

translations.literal: Given academician of the Guanwen Hall, prefect of Qingyuan, and coastal military commissioner, he again did not accept and was again granted a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to academician of the Guanwen Hall while also appointed prefect of Qingyuan and coastal military commissioner, he declined once more and was again granted a ceremonial post.

sentences.zh: 乃以資政殿大學士充萬壽觀使。

translations.literal: He was then made grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表上，帝輟朝，特贈少保。

translations.literal: He died; his final memorial was submitted; the Emperor suspended court and specially posthumously granted him Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his final memorial was submitted; the emperor suspended court and specially posthumously granted him the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 棟之學本諸周、程氏，負海內重望。

translations.literal: Dong’s learning traced to the Zhou and Cheng schools; he bore great renown throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Dong’s learning derived from the Zhou and Cheng masters, and he enjoyed great renown throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 方賈似道入相，登用故老，列之從官，棟亦預焉。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao entered the chancellorship he elevated old worthies and listed them among attendant officials; Dong was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao became chief councilor he brought back veteran statesmen and placed them among the attendant officials; Dong was among them.

sentences.zh: 及彗星見，棟乃言蚩尤旗，非彗也，故為世所少云。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared Dong said it was the Banner of Chiyou, not a comet; hence he is little spoken of by the world.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared Dong declared it was the Banner of Chiyou, not a comet—hence he is seldom praised by later ages.

sentences.zh: 或謂棟姑為是言，陰告於帝，謀逐似道，似道覺之，遂蒙疑而去。

translations.literal: Some said Dong spoke thus only nominally, secretly informing the Emperor to plot expelling Sidao; Sidao learned of it and Dong came under suspicion and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Dong made that claim only for show while secretly informing the emperor of a plan to drive Sidao out; Sidao learned of it, Dong fell under suspicion, and he left office.

sentences.zh: 所著有《崇道集》、《平舟文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Collected Works on Honoring the Way and the Collected Works of the Level Boat.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Collected Works on Honoring the Way and the Collected Works of the Level Boat.

sentences.zh: 姚希得

translations.literal: Yao Xide
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide

sentences.zh: 姚希得，字逢原，一字叔剛，潼川人，嘉定十六年進士。

translations.literal: Yao Xide, style name Fengyuan, also styled Shugang, was a man of Tongchuan and a jinshi of the sixteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide, whose style was Fengyuan and who also went by Shugang, came from Tongchuan and passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of the Jiading reign.

sentences.zh: 授小溪主簿，待次三年，朝夕討論《六經》、諸子百家之言。

translations.literal: He was appointed registrar of Xiaoxi; during three years awaiting assignment he discussed morning and evening the Six Classics and the words of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed registrar of Xiaoxi, he spent three years awaiting assignment studying the Six Classics and the writings of the hundred schools from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 調盤石令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Panshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Panshi.

sentences.zh: 會蜀有兵難，軍需調度不擾而集，更調嘉定府司理參軍。

translations.literal: When Shu had military troubles, he gathered army supplies without disturbance and was transferred to judicial administrator of Jiading prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When military troubles broke out in Shu, he mobilized army supplies without disturbing the people and was transferred to judicial administrator of Jiading prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改知蒲江縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Pujiang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Pujiang county.

sentences.zh: 巨室挾勢，邑號難治。

translations.literal: Great clans wielded power; the county was known as hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful clans threw their weight around, and the county had a reputation for being hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 希得綏強扶弱，聲聞著聞。

translations.literal: Xide soothed the strong and supported the weak; his fame became outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Xide restrained the strong and aided the weak, and his reputation became widely known.

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院事遊似以希得名聞，召審察，遷行在都進奏院，通判太平州，改福州，徒步至候官，吏不知為通判也。

translations.literal: Vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs You Si, hearing Xide’s fame, summoned him for review; he was transferred to the capital Memorial Transmission Office, deputy prefect of Taiping, then Fuzhou; he walked on foot to Houguan and the clerks did not know he was the deputy prefect.
translations.idiomatic: You Si, vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, heard of Xide’s reputation, summoned him for review, and had him transferred to the capital Memorial Transmission Office and then as deputy prefect of Taiping; reassigned to Fuzhou, he walked on foot to Houguan, and the clerks did not even realize he was the deputy prefect.

sentences.zh: 召為國子監丞，遷太府寺丞，時暫書擬金部文字兼沂靖王府教授。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Education, promoted vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and for a time drafted documents for the Revenue Section while also instructor at the Prince of Yi Jing estate.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Education, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and for a time drafted documents for the Revenue Section while also serving as instructor at the Prince of Yi Jing’s household.

sentences.zh: 時帝斥逐權奸，收召名德，舉朝相慶。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor expelled powerful traitors and recalled men of renown; the whole court rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was expelling powerful traitors and recalling men of renown; the whole court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 希得以為外觀形狀，似若清明之朝；

translations.literal: Xide considered that outward appearance and form resembled a clear and bright court;
translations.idiomatic: Xide thought that outwardly the court looked bright and orderly;

sentences.zh: 內察脈息，有類危亡之證。

translations.literal: inwardly examining the pulse, there were signs resembling those of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: but when he felt the pulse within, it bore the signs of a state nearing collapse.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏言：「堯、舜、三代之時，無危亡之事，而常喜危亡之言；

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized: 'In the age of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties there were no affairs of peril and ruin, yet they always welcomed words of peril and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial: “In the age of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties there were no crises of collapse, yet rulers always welcomed talk of crisis;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，多危亡之事，而常諱危亡之言。

translations.literal: from Qin and Han onward there have been many affairs of peril and ruin, yet they always taboo words of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: from Qin and Han onward there have been many collapses, yet rulers constantly taboo such talk.

sentences.zh: 夫危亡之事不可有，而危亡之言不可亡。

translations.literal: Affairs of peril and ruin must not exist, but words of peril and ruin must not perish.
translations.idiomatic: The events of collapse must not be allowed to happen, but the language of collapse must never be allowed to die out.

sentences.zh: 後世人主乃履危如履坦，諱言如諱病。」

translations.literal: Later rulers tread peril as if on level ground and taboo words as they taboo illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors walk through danger as if on level ground and avoid such words as they avoid naming a disease.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「君子非不收召，而意向猶未調一；

translations.literal: He also said: 'Worthies are not unreceived, yet intentions are still not harmonized into one;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Worthy men are indeed being recalled, yet minds are still not united in one purpose;

sentences.zh: 小人非不斥逐，而根株猶未痛斷。

translations.literal: petty men are not undriven out, yet their roots and stems are still not painfully severed.
translations.idiomatic: petty men are indeed being driven out, yet their roots have not been cut to the quick.

sentences.zh: 大權若操握，而不能無旁蹊曲逕之疑；

translations.literal: Great power seems grasped, yet one cannot be without suspicion of side paths and crooked byways;
translations.idiomatic: Supreme power seems firmly held, yet suspicion remains that side doors and crooked paths still exist;

sentences.zh: 大勢若更張，而未見有長治久安之道。

translations.literal: the great trend seems renewed, yet no way of long order and lasting peace is seen.
translations.idiomatic: the great course seems to be changing, yet no path to lasting peace and stability is in sight.

sentences.zh: 廷臣之所諷諫，封囊之所奏陳，非不激切，而陛下固不之罪，亦不之行。

translations.literal: What court ministers admonish and what sealed memorials present is not without urgency, yet Your Majesty neither punishes nor carries them out.
translations.idiomatic: The admonitions of court ministers and the memorials in sealed packets are not lacking in urgency, yet Your Majesty neither punishes the speakers nor acts on what they say.

sentences.zh: 自古甘蹈危亡之機，非獨暗主，而明君亦有焉，此臣之所甚懼。

translations.literal: From antiquity those who willingly tread the brink of peril and ruin are not only benighted rulers; enlightened rulers have them too—this is what this subject greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity those who willingly court the brink of ruin are not only benighted rulers—enlightened rulers have done so as well. That is what I fear most.

sentences.zh: 朝廷者，萬化之所自出也，實根於人君之一心。

translations.literal: The court is where the myriad transformations issue forth; it truly roots in the sovereign’s single heart.
translations.idiomatic: The court is where the myriad transformations of state originate; it truly takes root in the sovereign’s single heart.

sentences.zh: 夫何大明當天，猶有可議者？

translations.literal: How is it that with great brightness dominating the sky there are still matters open to debate?
translations.idiomatic: How can it be that with such brightness shining over the realm, there are still matters open to dispute?

sentences.zh: 內小學之建，人皆知陛下有意建儲也。

translations.literal: The establishment of the inner elementary school—everyone knows Your Majesty intends to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: The founding of the inner elementary school—everyone knows Your Majesty intends to establish an heir.

sentences.zh: 然歲月逾邁，未睹施行，人心危疑，無所系屬。

translations.literal: Yet years pass beyond measure without implementation seen; people’s hearts are perilous and doubtful, with nothing to attach to.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the years go by with no sign of action; hearts are anxious and doubtful, with nothing to hold them steady.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢而下，嗣不蚤定，事出倉卒，或宮闈出令，或宦寺主謀，或奸臣首議，此皆足以危人之國也。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, when succession was not early fixed affairs came in haste—sometimes orders from the inner palace, sometimes eunuchs directing plots, sometimes treacherous ministers initiating counsel—all enough to endanger a man’s state.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, whenever succession was not settled early, events erupted in haste—sometimes orders from the inner palace, sometimes eunuchs directing the plot, sometimes treacherous ministers leading the counsel—all enough to endanger a state.

sentences.zh: 陛下何憚而不蚤定大計？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty shrink from not early fixing the great plan?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty hesitate to settle this great matter early?

sentences.zh: 邸第之盛，人皆知篤於親愛也。

translations.literal: The splendor of princely mansions—everyone knows Your Majesty is devoted to kinship love.
translations.idiomatic: The grandeur of the princely mansions—everyone knows Your Majesty is devoted to your kin.

sentences.zh: 然依馮者眾，輕視王法，請托之行，捷於影響。

translations.literal: Yet those who rely on patronage are many; they slight royal law; the running of requests moves faster than shadow following form.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who lean on patronage are many; they treat the royal law lightly, and favor-seeking moves faster than a shadow.

sentences.zh: 楊幹，晉侯弟也，亂行於曲梁，而魏絳戮其仆，晉侯始怒而終悔，晉卒以霸。

translations.literal: Yang Gan, younger brother of the Marquis of Jin, committed disorderly conduct at Qu Liang; Wei Jiang executed his servant; the Marquis of Jin was first angry but finally repented, and Jin in the end achieved hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gan, younger brother of the Marquis of Jin, committed an outrage at Qu Liang; Wei Jiang executed his servant. The marquis was angry at first but repented in the end, and Jin ultimately achieved hegemony.

sentences.zh: 平原君，趙王弟也，不出租稅，而趙奢刑其用事者，趙王賢而用之，趙卒以強。

translations.literal: Lord Pingyuan, younger brother of the King of Zhao, paid no rent or tax; Zhao She punished those who acted for him; the King of Zhao esteemed and employed him, and Zhao in the end grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pingyuan, younger brother of the King of Zhao, paid no rent or tax; Zhao She punished those who acted in his name. The king recognized his worth and employed him, and Zhao ultimately grew strong.

sentences.zh: 皆足以興人之國也。

translations.literal: All were enough to raise a man’s state.
translations.idiomatic: Both cases were enough to revive a state.

sentences.zh: 陛下何為而不少伸國法？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty act and not slightly extend royal law?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty not enforce the royal law even a little?

sentences.zh: 今女冠者流，眾所指目；

translations.literal: Now the female Daoist priest and her kind are what the multitude points at;
translations.idiomatic: Today the female Daoist priests are what everyone points at;

sentences.zh: 近璫小臣，時竊威福。

translations.literal: nearby eunuchs and petty officials at times steal authority and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: nearby eunuchs and petty officials steal authority and favor at will.

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下之心乍明乍晦之所致，豈不謂之危乎？

translations.literal: All these come from Your Majesty’s heart now bright now dim—is this not called peril?
translations.idiomatic: All this comes from Your Majesty’s heart flickering between clarity and obscurity—is this not peril?

sentences.zh: 國有善類，猶人有元氣，善類一敗一消，元氣一病一衰。

translations.literal: A state has good types as a man has primordial qi; good types fail and vanish one by one, primordial qi sickens and declines one bout at a time.
translations.idiomatic: A state has worthy men as a person has vital breath; with each worthy man defeated and removed, vital breath sickens and wanes.

sentences.zh: 善類能幾，豈堪數消，消極則國隨之矣。

translations.literal: How many good types can there be—how can they bear repeated vanishing? When vanishing reaches its limit the state follows.
translations.idiomatic: How many worthy men are there? They cannot bear to be worn away again and again; when they are exhausted, the state follows.

sentences.zh: 陛下明於知人，公於用人，固無權奸再用之意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is clear in knowing men and fair in employing them; you certainly have no intent to reuse powerful traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is discerning in knowing men and fair in employing them; you certainly have no wish to bring powerful traitors back.

sentences.zh: 然道路之人往往竊議，此元祐、紹聖將分之機也。

translations.literal: Yet people on the roads often whisper in private—this is the moment when Yuanyou and Shaosheng will divide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people on the roads whisper among themselves—this is the moment when factions like those of Yuanyou and Shaosheng threaten to split apart again.

sentences.zh: 禍根猶伏而未去，不幾於安其危乎？」

translations.literal: The roots of disaster still lie hidden and have not gone—is this not nearly settling in one’s peril?
translations.idiomatic: The roots of disaster still lie hidden and have not been removed—is this not nearly treating danger as safety?”

sentences.zh: 帝改容曰：「朕決不用史嵩之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed expression and said: 'I will certainly not employ Shi Songzhi.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s expression changed and he said, “I will certainly never employ Shi Songzhi again.”

sentences.zh: 遷知大宗正丞兼權金部郎官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court concurrently acting director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court while also serving as acting director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 李韶以病告，十上疏欲去。

translations.literal: Li Shao reported illness and ten times memorialized wishing to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao reported illness and submitted ten memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 希得言：「韶有德望，雖以病告，曷若留奉內祠，侍經幄，亦足為朝廷重。」

translations.literal: Xide said: 'Shao has virtue and renown; though he reports illness, how much better to retain him in an inner sinecure, attending the classics curtain— that too is enough to weight the court.'
translations.idiomatic: Xide said, “Shao has virtue and standing; though he reports illness, how much better to keep him in an inner ceremonial post, attending the classics curtain—that alone would add weight to the court.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「財用困竭，民生憔悴，移此不急之費，以實軍儲，以厚民生，敬天莫大於此，豈在崇大宮宇，莊嚴設像哉！」

translations.literal: He also said: 'Revenue is exhausted and the people’s livelihood is withered; shift these non-urgent expenses to fill army stores and enrich the people’s livelihood—nothing greater in honoring Heaven than this; is it in enlarging palaces and solemnly setting up images?'
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “Revenue is exhausted and the people are worn down. Shift these non-urgent expenses to fill the army stores and relieve the people—nothing honors Heaven more than this. Is reverence found in enlarging palaces and setting up ornate images?”

sentences.zh: 又條救錢楮三策，請置惠民局，帝皆以為可行。

translations.literal: He also listed three policies to save paper money, requested establishing a Bureau to Benefit the People, and the Emperor deemed all feasible.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth three policies to rescue paper currency and asked that a Bureau to Benefit the People be established; the emperor deemed all of them feasible.

sentences.zh: 進秘書丞，尋遷著作郎，授江西提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director of the Secretariat, soon promoted compiler, and appointed Jiangxi intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, soon to compiler, and appointed Jiangxi intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 役法久壞，臨川富室有賂吏求免者，希得竟罪之。

translations.literal: The corvée law had long been broken; wealthy families of Linchuan bribed clerks seeking exemption; Xide in the end punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The corvée law had long been in ruins; wealthy families in Linchuan bribed clerks to seek exemption, and Xide punished them to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 遂提點刑獄，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was then made judicial intendant and given direct appointment to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made judicial intendant and given direct appointment to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加度支員外郎，尋直寶章閣，移治贛州。

translations.literal: Before long he was given outer vice director of the Revenue Section, soon direct appointment to the Baozhang Pavilion, and transferred to govern Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given the rank of outer vice director of the Revenue Section, soon direct appointment to the Baozhang Pavilion, and transferred to govern Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜有偽號「崔太尉」者，據石壁，連結數郡；

translations.literal: Among bandits was one with the false title 'Grand Marshal Cui' who held Shibi and linked several prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Among the bandits was one who took the false title “Grand Marshal Cui,” held Shibi, and linked several prefectures;

sentences.zh: 劉老龍等聚眾焚掠，一方繹騷。

translations.literal: Liu Laolong and others gathered crowds to burn and plunder, and one region was in continuous uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laolong and others gathered mobs to burn and plunder, throwing the whole region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 希得指授方略，不五旬平之。

translations.literal: Xide directed strategy; in less than fifty days he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Xide laid out the strategy, and in less than fifty days the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 以直寶謨閣、廣西轉運判官兼權靜江府。

translations.literal: He was given direct appointment to the Baomo Pavilion, made Guangxi transport deputy commissioner, and concurrent acting prefect of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given direct appointment to the Baomo Pavilion, appointed Guangxi transport deputy commissioner, and concurrently acting prefect of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋授直徽猷閣、知靜江府、主管廣西經略安撫司公事兼轉運判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was given direct appointment to the Huiyou Pavilion, made prefect of Jingjiang, superintendent of Guangxi military commission affairs, and transport deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given direct appointment to the Huiyou Pavilion, appointed prefect of Jingjiang and superintendent of Guangxi military commission affairs while also serving as transport deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 母喪，免。

translations.literal: His mother died and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office for mourning.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書少監兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat concurrently rectifier of all bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat while also serving as rectifier of all bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入對，言君子小人邪正之辯，且曰：「君子犯顏敢諫，拂陛下之意，退甘家食，此乃為國計，非為身計也。

translations.literal: At audience he spoke on the debate between worthies and petty men, orthodox and heterodox, and said: 'Worthies offend the countenance and dare remonstrate, going against Your Majesty’s intent and retiring content with family fare—this is planning for the state, not for the person.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he spoke on the distinction between worthies and petty men, the upright and the corrupt, saying, “Worthy men risk your displeasure and dare to remonstrate, going against your wishes and retiring content with a modest home life—this is for the sake of the state, not for themselves.

sentences.zh: 小人自植朋黨，擠排正人，甘言佞語，一切順陛下之意，遂取陛下官爵，此乃為身計，非為國計也。」

translations.literal: Petty men plant factions of their own, crowd out upright men, use sweet words and flattery, entirely follow Your Majesty’s intent, and thereby seize Your Majesty’s offices and ranks—this is planning for the person, not for the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Petty men build factions of their own, drive out upright men, and with sweet flattery do whatever pleases you, thereby winning your offices and ranks—for themselves, not for the state.”

sentences.zh: 遷宗正少卿兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼權給事中，兼權刑部侍郎、同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, concurrently compiler of the National History and examiner of the Veritable Records, acting drafting censor, acting vice minister of Justice, and co-compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court while also compiling the National History and examining the Veritable Records, serving as acting drafting censor and acting vice minister of Justice, and co-compiling the National History and Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 時西方用兵，有為嵩之復出計者，謂非此人不能辦。

translations.literal: At the time the west was at war; some plotted Songzhi’s return, saying no one but this man could manage it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time war was raging in the west; some plotted to bring Songzhi back, claiming that no one else could handle the crisis.

sentences.zh: 帝有意再用，知希得必執之，出旨諭意，希得毅然具疏密奏，不報。

translations.literal: The Emperor intended to employ him again; knowing Xide would certainly oppose it, he issued an edict stating his intent; Xide resolutely submitted a secret memorial in full; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to employ Songzhi again; knowing Xide would certainly oppose it, he issued an edict stating his intent. Xide resolutely submitted a full secret memorial, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 又繳鄧泳予祠之命。

translations.literal: He also returned the order granting Deng Yong a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He also returned the order granting Deng Yong a ceremonial post.

sentences.zh: 右正言邵澤、監察御史吳衍、殿中侍御史朱熠相繼論罷。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Shao Ze, investigating censor Wu Yan, and palace censor Zhu Yi in succession impeached him and he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officer Shao Ze, the investigating censor Wu Yan, and the palace censor Zhu Yi impeached him in succession until he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，以集英殿修撰提點千秋鴻禧觀。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 未幾，依舊職兩淮宣撫使司判官，俄加寶謨閣待制，移京西、湖南北、四川。

translations.literal: Before long, at his former rank, he was made administrative aide of the Two Huai pacification commission; soon given attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and transferred to Jingxi, Hunan North, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed at his former rank as administrative aide of the Two Huai pacification commission; soon promoted to attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and transferred to Jingxi, Hunan North, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔敘復元官。

translations.literal: An edict restored his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his original rank.

sentences.zh: 護江陵有功，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He had merit in defending Jiangling and was summoned as vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in defending Jiangling he was summoned as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「姚希得才望可為閫帥。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Yao Xide’s talent and renown qualify him to be a frontier commander.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Yao Xide’s talent and standing qualify him to command on the frontier.”

sentences.zh: 乃進煥章閣待制、知慶元府、沿海制置使，繼升敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to attendant of the Huanzhang Pavilion, prefect of Qingyuan, and coastal military commissioner, and soon promoted to attendant of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to attendant of the Huanzhang Pavilion, appointed prefect of Qingyuan and coastal military commissioner, and soon advanced to attendant of the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詔增沿海舟師，希得為之廣募水軍，造戰艦，蓄糧食，蠲米一萬二千石、舊逋一百萬。

translations.literal: An edict increased coastal naval forces; Xide for this widely recruited sailors, built warships, stored grain, and remitted twelve thousand piculs of grain and one million in old arrears.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the coastal fleet enlarged, Xide widely recruited sailors, built warships, and stockpiled grain; he also remitted twelve thousand piculs of grain and one million in old arrears.

sentences.zh: 去官，庫余羨悉以代民輸。

translations.literal: When he left office, all surplus in the treasury he used to pay the people’s levies in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he used the entire treasury surplus to pay the people’s levies on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 召為工部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of Works and reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of Works and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 入侍經筵，帝問慶元之政甚悉。

translations.literal: Attending the classics lecture, the Emperor questioned him in detail on Qingyuan administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics lecture the emperor questioned him in detail about his administration in Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以華文閣直學士、沿江制置使知建康府、江東安撫使、行宮留守。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Huawen Hall, riverine military commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, and resident commissioner of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Huawen Hall, riverine military commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, and resident commissioner of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 希得按行江上，慰勞士卒，眾皆歡說。

translations.literal: Xide inspected along the river, comforted and rewarded the troops, and all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Xide toured the river line, comforted and rewarded the troops, and the men were all delighted.

sentences.zh: 溧陽饑，發稟勸分，全活者眾。

translations.literal: When Liyang suffered famine he opened granaries and urged sharing; many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyang suffered famine he opened the granaries and urged mutual relief, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 創寧江軍，自建康、太平至池州列砦置屋二萬餘間，屯戍七千餘人。

translations.literal: He founded the Ningjiang Army, from Jiankang and Taiping to Chizhou lining forts and setting up more than twenty thousand rooms, garrisoning more than seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Ningjiang Army, building more than twenty thousand quarters in a chain of forts from Jiankang and Taiping to Chizhou, with a garrison of more than seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，一再降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and repeatedly issued edicts of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he repeatedly issued edicts of praise.

sentences.zh: 加寶章閣學士，尋加刑部尚書，依舊任兼淮西總領。

translations.literal: He was given academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, soon minister of Justice, continuing in his post while also Huai West general superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, soon promoted to minister of Justice while continuing in his post and also serving as Huai West general superintendent.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，召為兵部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding he was summoned as minister of War and reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Jingding reign he was summoned as minister of War and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 乃言用人才、修政事、治兵甲、惜財用四事。

translations.literal: He then spoke on four matters: employing talent, repairing government, managing arms and armor, and cherishing revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke on four matters: employing talent, repairing government, managing arms and armor, and husbanding revenue.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and guest of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 公星變，上疏引咎，乞解機務。

translations.literal: When the Duke Star changed he memorialized taking blame and begged to be relieved of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke Star changed he submitted a memorial taking blame and asked to be relieved of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: He was concurrently acting vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently appointed acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，授同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，尋授參知政事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong acceded he was given vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, soon appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong acceded to the throne he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, and soon made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以言罷，授資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was removed on impeachment and given academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed after impeachment, he was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知潭州、湖南安撫使，以疾甚，辭，乃仍舊職奉祠。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan pacification commissioner; his illness was severe and he declined; he was then again granted a sinecure at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan pacification commissioner, he declined because his illness was severe and was again granted a ceremonial post at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 請致仕，詔不許，力請，以資政殿大學士、金紫光祿大夫、依舊潼川郡公致仕。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; an edict did not permit it; he pressed the request and retired as grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, Grandee of the Golden Girdle and Purple Purity, and Duke of Tongchuan at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire; the emperor refused, but when he pressed the request he was allowed to retire as grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, Grandee of the Golden Girdle and Purple Purity, and Duke of Tongchuan at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 咸淳五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianchun reign he died.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝輟朝，贈少保。

translations.literal: When his final memorial was heard the Emperor suspended court and posthumously granted him Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived the emperor suspended court and posthumously granted him the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 希得忠亮平實，清儉自將，好引善類，不要虛譽，蓋有誦薦於上而其人莫之知者。

translations.literal: Xide was loyal, bright, even, and plain; frugal in his own conduct; fond of recommending good types; disdaining empty renown—there were those he praised and recommended above while the persons themselves did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Xide was loyal, upright, even-tempered, and plain; he lived frugally, delighted in recommending worthy men, and scorned empty fame—often praising someone to the throne while the man himself never knew.

sentences.zh: 廣西官署以錦為帟幕，希得曰：「吾起身書生安用此！」

translations.literal: Guangxi official quarters used brocade for curtains and screens; Xide said: 'I rose from a mere scholar—what use have I for this!'
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi official quarters used brocade for curtains and screens. Xide said, “I rose from a mere scholar—what use have I for this!”

sentences.zh: 命以繒纈易之。

translations.literal: He ordered it exchanged for plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them replaced with plain silk.

sentences.zh: 蜀之親族姻舊相依者數十家，希得廩之終身，昏喪悉損己力，晚年計口授田，各有差。

translations.literal: Several tens of families of Shu kin and old affines depended on him; Xide provisioned them for life; weddings and funerals he all bore from his own strength; in later years he allotted fields by mouth, each with its difference.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen families of Shu relatives and old friends depended on him; Xide supported them for life, paid for all their weddings and funerals from his own purse, and in his later years allotted fields to each according to their needs.

sentences.zh: 所著有《續言行錄》、《奏稿》、《橘州文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Continued Record of Words and Deeds, Memorial Drafts, and the Collected Works of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Continued Record of Words and Deeds, Memorial Drafts, and the Collected Works of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 包恢，字宏父，建昌人。

translations.literal: Bao Hui, style name Hongfu, was a man of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui, whose style was Hongfu, came from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 自其父揚、世父約、叔父遜從朱熹、陸九淵學。

translations.literal: From his father Yang, his father’s elder brother Yue, and his father’s younger brother Xun, he studied with Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang, his uncle Yue, and his uncle Xun had all studied with Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 恢少為諸父門人講《大學》，其言高明，諸父驚焉。

translations.literal: When young Hui lectured on the Great Learning to his uncles’ disciples, his words were lofty and bright and the uncles were startled.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hui lectured on the Great Learning to his uncles’ disciples; his exposition was so penetrating that his uncles were astonished.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Jiading reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調金谿主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to registrar of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed registrar of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 邵武守王遂辟光澤主簿，平寇亂。

translations.literal: Shaowu prefect Wang Sui invited him as registrar of Guangze and he pacified bandit turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, prefect of Shaowu, invited him to serve as registrar of Guangze, where he pacified bandit unrest.

sentences.zh: 建寧守袁甫薦為府學教授，監虎翼軍，募土豪討唐石之寇。

translations.literal: Jianning prefect Yuan Fu recommended him as prefectural school instructor, supervised the Tiger Wing Army, and recruited local strongmen to attack the Tang Shi bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu, prefect of Jianning, recommended him as prefectural school instructor; he supervised the Tiger Wing Army and recruited local militia to attack the Tang Shi bandits.

sentences.zh: 授掌故，改沿海制置司幹官。

translations.literal: He was appointed record keeper and changed to staff officer of the coastal military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed record keeper, he was transferred to staff officer of the coastal military commission.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，盜起金壇、溧陽之間，恢部諸將為十誅夷之。

translations.literal: When famine struck, bandits rose between Jintan and Liyang; Hui deployed generals and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, bandits rose between Jintan and Liyang; Hui deployed his generals and exterminated them.

sentences.zh: 沿江制置使陳韡辟為機宜，復有平寇功，改知吉州永豐縣，未行，差發運幹官。

translations.literal: Riverine military commissioner Chen Kai invited him as confidential aide; he again had merit pacifying bandits; he was changed to magistrate of Yongfeng in Jizhou but did not go; he was assigned transport staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai, riverine military commissioner, invited him as confidential aide; he again distinguished himself pacifying bandits; appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Jizhou, he did not take up the post and was instead assigned as transport staff officer.

sentences.zh: 福建安撫使陳塏檄平寇，遷武學諭、宗正寺主簿，添差通判臺州。

translations.literal: Fujian pacification commissioner Chen Kai ordered him to pacify bandits; he was promoted military instructor and registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, and given additional assignment as deputy prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai, Fujian pacification commissioner, ordered him to pacify bandits; he was promoted to military instructor and registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, with additional assignment as deputy prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 徐鹿卿討溫寇，辟兼提點刑獄司主管文字，議收捕。

translations.literal: Xu Luqing campaigned against Wen bandits and invited him concurrently as chief clerk of the judicial commission, deliberating capture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Luqing campaigned against the Wen bandits he invited Hui as chief clerk of the judicial commission to plan their capture.

sentences.zh: 改通判臨安府，遷宗正寺主簿、知臺州。

translations.literal: He was changed to deputy prefect of Lin’an, promoted registrar of the Imperial Clan Court and prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to deputy prefect of Lin’an, he was promoted to registrar of the Imperial Clan Court and prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 有妖僧居山中，號「活佛」，男女爭事之，因為奸利，豪貴風靡，恢誅其僧。

translations.literal: A sorcerer monk lived in the mountains styled "Living Buddha"; men and women vied to serve him; he thereby sought illicit profit and the powerful followed like wind; Hui executed the monk.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer monk in the mountains styled himself "Living Buddha"; men and women vied to serve him, and through them he sought illicit profit until the powerful all followed his lead; Hui had the monk executed.

sentences.zh: 進左司郎官，未行，改湖北提點刑獄，未行，移福建兼知建寧。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Division director but did not go; changed to Hubei judicial intendant but did not go; transferred to Fujian while also governing Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Division director, he did not take up the post; reassigned as Hubei judicial intendant, he again did not go; he was transferred to Fujian while also governing Jianning.

sentences.zh: 閩俗以九月祠「五王」生日，靡金帛，傾市奉之。

translations.literal: Fujian custom in the ninth month sacrifices to the birthday of the "Five Kings," squandering gold and silk; the whole market turns out to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian custom held that in the ninth month people sacrificed to the birthday of the "Five Kings," squandering gold and silk as the whole market turned out to worship them.

sentences.zh: 恢曰：「彼非犬豕，安得一日而五子同生，非不祥者乎？

translations.literal: Hui said: 'They are not dogs or pigs—how could five sons be born on one day? Is this not inauspicious?
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, “They are not dogs or pigs—how could five sons be born on the same day? Is that not an ill omen?

sentences.zh: 而尊畏之若是。」

translations.literal: Yet you honor and fear them thus.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet you honor and fear them as you do.”

sentences.zh: 眾感悟，為之衰止。

translations.literal: The multitude were awakened and for this the practice declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were moved and the practice died away.

sentences.zh: 兼轉運判官，以侍御史周坦論罷。

translations.literal: Concurrently transport deputy commissioner, he was removed on impeachment by attendant censor Zhou Tan.
translations.idiomatic: While also serving as transport deputy commissioner, he was dismissed after impeachment by the attendant censor Zhou Tan.

sentences.zh: 光州布衣陳景夏上書云：「包恢剛正不屈之臣，言者汙蔑之耳。」

translations.literal: Guangzhou commoner Chen Jingxia memorialized: 'Bao Hui is a minister upright and unyielding; the speakers merely slander him.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxia, a commoner of Guangzhou, memorialized: “Bao Hui is an upright and unyielding minister; his accusers merely slander him.”

sentences.zh: 又四年，起為廣東轉運判官，權經略使，遷侍右郎官，尋為大理少卿，即日除直顯文閣、浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Four years later he was recalled as Guangdong transport deputy commissioner and acting military commissioner, promoted Right Attendant Division director, soon vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and the same day given direct appointment to the Xianwen Pavilion and made Zhexi judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was recalled as Guangdong transport deputy commissioner and acting military commissioner, promoted to Right Attendant Division director, soon appointed vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and the same day given direct appointment to the Xianwen Pavilion and made Zhexi judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 是時海寇為亂，恢單車就道、調許、澉浦分屯建砦，一旦集諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: At the time sea bandits were in turmoil; Hui went alone by carriage on the road, deployed troops at Xu and Ganpu in separate camps building forts, and in one day gathered all armies to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits were then in revolt; Hui went alone to take up his post, deployed troops at Xu and Ganpu in separate camps, and in a single day gathered all forces and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 嘉興吏因和糴受賕百萬，恢被旨慮囚，曰：「吾用此消沴氣。」

translations.literal: A Jiaxing clerk took a million in bribes through harmonized purchase; Hui received orders to review prisoners and said: 'I use this to dispel malign qi.'
translations.idiomatic: A Jiaxing clerk had taken a million in bribes through the harmonized-purchase system; ordered to review the case, Hui said, “I will use this to dispel the malign influence.”

sentences.zh: 乃減死，斷其手。

translations.literal: He therefore reduced the death penalty and cut off his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He commuted the death sentence and had the man’s hand cut off.

sentences.zh: 進直龍圖閣、權發運，升秘閣修撰，知隆興府兼江西轉運。

translations.literal: He was advanced with direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall and acting transport commissioner, promoted compiler of the Secretariat, prefect of Longxing, and Jiangxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted with direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall and acting transport commissioner, he was advanced to compiler of the Secretariat, appointed prefect of Longxing, and made Jiangxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沈妖妓於水，化為狐，人皆神之。

translations.literal: He drowned a sorceress in the water; she transformed into a fox and people all regarded it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned a sorceress in the water; she was said to have turned into a fox, and people regarded the deed as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 有母訴子者，年月後狀作「疏」字，恢疑之，呼其子至，泣不言。

translations.literal: A mother sued her son; years later the petition formed the character 'sparse'; Hui suspected this, called the son before him, and he wept without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: A mother sued her son; years later the petition formed the character for “sparse”; Hui grew suspicious, summoned the son, and the boy wept without speaking.

sentences.zh: 及得其情，母孀居，與僧通，惡其子諫，以不孝坐之，狀則僧為之也。

translations.literal: When he got the facts: the mother lived as widow and had relations with a monk; she hated her son’s remonstrance and had him convicted of unfilial conduct; the petition was written by the monk.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the truth: the widowed mother was having an affair with a monk; she hated her son’s remonstrance and had him convicted of unfilial conduct on a petition the monk had written.

sentences.zh: 因責子侍養跬步不離，僧無由至。

translations.literal: He therefore charged the son to attend and nurture her, not leaving her by a step, so the monk had no way to come.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the son to attend his mother constantly, never leaving her side, so the monk could no longer gain access.

sentences.zh: 母乃托夫諱日，入寺作佛事，以籠盛衣帛，因納僧於內以歸。

translations.literal: The mother then used her husband’s taboo day, entered a temple for Buddhist rites, used a cage holding clothes and silk, and thereby put the monk inside to bring home.
translations.idiomatic: The mother then used her husband’s taboo day to enter a temple for Buddhist rites, placed clothes and silk in a cage, and smuggled the monk inside it back to her home.

sentences.zh: 恢知之，使人要之，置籠公庫，逾旬，吏報籠中臭達於外，恢命沉於江，語其子曰：「為汝除此害矣。」

translations.literal: Hui learned of it, sent men to intercept her, placed the cage in the public storehouse; after ten days clerks reported stench from the cage reached outside; Hui ordered it sunk in the river and told the son: 'I have removed this harm for you.'
translations.idiomatic: Hui learned of it, sent men to intercept her, and placed the cage in the public storehouse; after ten days clerks reported that the stench reached outside; Hui ordered it sunk in the river and told the son, “I have removed this scourge for you.”

sentences.zh: 又姑死者假子婦棺以斂，家貧不能償，婦於恢，恢怒，買一棺，紿其婦臥棺中以試，就掩而葬之。

translations.literal: Again, when an aunt died she borrowed her daughter-in-law’s coffin for encoffining; the family was poor and could not repay; the daughter-in-law complained to Hui; Hui was angry, bought a coffin, deceived the daughter-in-law into lying in the coffin to test it, and then covered and buried her.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, when an aunt died she borrowed her daughter-in-law’s coffin; the family was too poor to replace it and the daughter-in-law complained to Hui. Enraged, Hui bought a coffin, tricked the woman into lying in it to test the fit, and had her sealed inside and buried.

sentences.zh: 改湖南轉運使，罷。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hunan transport commissioner and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hunan transport commissioner, he was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景定初，拜大理卿、樞密都承旨兼侍講，權禮部侍郎，尋為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingding he was appointed chief of the Court of Judicial Review, chief receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs and lecturer-in-waiting, acting vice minister of Rites, soon drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingding reign he was appointed chief of the Court of Judicial Review, chief receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs and lecturer-in-waiting, acting vice minister of Rites, and soon drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 林希逸奏恢守法奉公，其心如水。

translations.literal: Lin Xiyi memorialized that Hui observed law and served the public; his heart was like water.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiyi memorialized that Hui observed the law and served the public faithfully, and that his heart was clear as water.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，進華文閣直學士、知平江府兼發運。

translations.literal: Acting vice minister of Justice, he was advanced to academician of the Huawen Hall, prefect of Pingjiang, and transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice minister of Justice he was advanced to academician of the Huawen Hall, appointed prefect of Pingjiang, and made transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 豪有奪民包舉田寄公租誣上者，恢上疏，指為以小民祈天永命之一事，帝覽奏惻然，罪任事者，即歸民田。

translations.literal: A powerful man seized commoners’ contracted fields and registered them as public rent to deceive above; Hui memorialized, pointing to this as one matter in which the little people pray Heaven for enduring mandate; the Emperor reading the memorial was moved, punished those in charge, and immediately returned the people’s fields.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful man had seized commoners’ contracted fields and registered them as public rent to deceive the throne; Hui memorialized, calling this a matter in which the common people pray Heaven for the dynasty’s enduring mandate. Reading the memorial, the emperor was moved, punished those responsible, and immediately returned the fields to the people.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，辭，改知紹興，又辭。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he declined; changed to govern Shaoxing, he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he declined; offered Shaoxing, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，召為刑部尚書，進端明殿學士，簽書樞密院事，封南城縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong acceded he was summoned as minister of Justice, advanced to academician of the Duanming Hall and signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed Marquis of Nancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong acceded he was summoned as minister of Justice, advanced to academician of the Duanming Hall and signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nancheng county.

sentences.zh: 郊祀禮成，還，以資政殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: When suburban sacrifice rites were completed he returned and retired as academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban sacrifice rites were completed he returned and retired as academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 恢歷仕所至，破豪猾，去奸吏，治蠱獄，課盆鹽，理銀欠，政聲赫然。

translations.literal: Wherever Hui served in his career he broke powerful scoundrels, removed corrupt officials, tried witchcraft cases, assessed basin salt, settled silver arrears—his governmental fame blazed bright.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Hui served he broke powerful scoundrels, removed corrupt officials, tried witchcraft cases, assessed basin salt, and settled silver arrears—his reputation for governance blazed bright.

sentences.zh: 嘗因輪對曰：「此臣心惻隱所以深切為陛下告者，陛下惻隱之心如天地日月，其閉而食之者曰近習、曰外戚耳。」

translations.literal: Once at rotating audience he said: 'This is what this subject’s compassionate heart deeply tells Your Majesty: Your Majesty’s compassionate heart is like heaven and earth, sun and moon; those who shut it in and feed on it are called close attendants and maternal kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Once at a rotating audience he said, “This is what my compassionate heart urgently tells you: your compassionate heart is like heaven and earth, sun and moon—but those who shut it in and feed on it are your close attendants and your maternal kin.”

sentences.zh: 參知政事董槐見而嘆曰：「吾等有慚色矣。」

translations.literal: Vice grand councilor Dong Huai seeing it sighed: 'We have cause for shame.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice grand councilor Dong Huai read it and sighed, “We ought to feel ashamed.”

sentences.zh: 他日講官因稱恢疏剴切，願容納。

translations.literal: Another day the lecturer praised Hui’s memorial as earnest and cutting and wished it might be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On another day a lecturer praised Hui’s memorial as earnest and incisive and urged that it be heeded.

sentences.zh: 理宗欣然曰：「其言甚直，朕何嘗怒直言！」

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong said with pleasure: 'His words are very straight—when have I ever been angry at straight speech!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong said with pleasure, “His words are very blunt—when have I ever been angry at blunt speech!”

sentences.zh: 經筵奏對，誠實懇惻，至身心之要，未嘗不從容諄至。

translations.literal: At the classics lecture and audience his words were sincere and earnest; on essentials of mind and body he was never without leisurely thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics lecture his answers were sincere and earnest; on essentials of mind and body he was always leisurely and thorough.

sentences.zh: 度宗至比恢為程顥、程頤。

translations.literal: Emperor Duzong even compared Hui to Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Duzong even compared Hui to Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 恢侍其父疾，滌濯掃除之役不命僮僕。

translations.literal: When Hui attended his father’s illness, washing and sweeping he did not command servants.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was ill Hui attended him himself, doing the washing and sweeping without calling on servants.

sentences.zh: 年八十有七，臨終，舉盧懷慎臥簀窮約事戒諸子斂以深衣，作書別親戚而後卒，有光隕其地。

translations.literal: At age eighty-seven, on his deathbed he cited Lu Huaishen’s lying on rush mat in poverty and simplicity, admonished his sons to encoffin him in deep garments, wrote letters bidding farewell to kin and then died; a light fell at that place.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-seven, on his deathbed he cited Lu Huaishen’s dying on a rush mat in poverty, admonished his sons to bury him in plain deep garments, wrote farewell letters to his kin, and then died; a light was seen to fall at the spot.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝輟朝，贈少保，謚文肅，賻銀絹五百。

translations.literal: When his final memorial was heard the Emperor suspended court, posthumously granted him Junior Guardian, gave the posthumous title Wensu, and bestowed five hundred in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived the emperor suspended court, posthumously granted him Junior Guardian, gave him the posthumous title Wensu, and bestowed five hundred in silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 常挺字方叔，福州人。

translations.literal: Chang Ting, style name Fangshu, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ting, whose style was Fangshu, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi of the second year of Jiaxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jiaxi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官為太學錄，召試館職，遷秘書省正字兼莊文府教授，升校書郎。

translations.literal: Through offices he was recorder of the Imperial Academy, summoned for examination for archive posts, promoted rectifier of the Secretariat concurrently instructor at the Zhuangwen estate, and advanced to collating editor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder of the Imperial Academy, was summoned for examination for archive posts, promoted to rectifier of the Secretariat while also instructing at the Zhuangwen estate, and advanced to collating editor.

sentences.zh: 輪對，乞以李若水配享高宗。

translations.literal: At rotating audience he begged that Li Ruoshui be given associated sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he asked that Li Ruoshui be granted associated sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 改秘書郎兼考功郎官，出知衢州，拜監察御史兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was changed to secretary concurrently director of the Merit Section, sent out as prefect of Quzhou, and appointed investigating censor concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to secretary while also serving as director of the Merit Section, he was sent out as prefect of Quzhou and appointed investigating censor while also lecturing at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 疏言邊閫三事：曰辟實才，曰奏實功，曰招實兵。

translations.literal: In a memorial he spoke of three matters for the frontier commands: namely recruiting real talent, reporting real achievements, and recruiting real soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he urged three reforms for the frontier commands: appoint men of genuine ability, report genuine achievements, and recruit genuine fighting men.

sentences.zh: 朝廷二事：曰選良吏，曰擢正人。

translations.literal: Two matters for the court: namely selecting good officials and promoting upright men.
translations.idiomatic: For the court he proposed two measures: choose capable officials and promote upright men.

sentences.zh: 又言：「願陛下深思宏遠之規模，奮發清明之志氣，立綱陳紀必為萬世之法程，昭德塞違以示百官之憲度。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'I hope Your Majesty will deeply ponder a grand and far-reaching design, rouse clear and bright resolve, establish standards and set forth regulations that must serve as models for ten thousand generations, and display virtue while blocking wrongdoing to show the law for the hundred officials.'
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “I pray Your Majesty will ponder a grand and far-reaching design, rouse a clear and resolute spirit, establish standards that will endure for ten thousand generations, and make virtue manifest while shutting out wrongdoing, so that the hundred officials may see the measure of the law.”

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿兼國子司業，兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼直舍人院。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrently vice chancellor of the Imperial University, concurrently compiler of the National History and examiner of the Veritable Records and reader-in-waiting at the drafts office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while also serving as vice chancellor of the Imperial University, compiler of the National History, examiner of the Veritable Records, and reader-in-waiting at the drafts office.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，權工部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was promoted palace attendant, acting vice minister of Works concurrently academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and made acting vice minister of Works while also serving as an academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice minister of Works and drafting censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works and appointed drafting censor.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫陳堯道論罷。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officer Chen Yaodao memorialized against him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after Right Remonstrance Officer Chen Yaodao impeached him.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣直學士知漳州，改知泉州，權兵部尚書兼侍讀，權禮部尚書兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: As direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he was made prefect of Zhangzhou, then transferred to Quanzhou; acting minister of War concurrently reader-in-waiting, acting minister of Rites concurrently co-compiler of the National History and co-author of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion and prefect of Zhangzhou, he was then transferred to Quanzhou; he served as acting minister of War and reader-in-waiting, and as acting minister of Rites while also co-compiling the National History and Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 進《帝學發題》，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He presented Topics for Imperial Learning and was promoted minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his Topics for Imperial Learning and was promoted to minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 咸淳三年，授同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，封合沙郡公，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun he was granted vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently acting vice grand councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Hesha Commandery, and appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianchun reign he was made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Hesha Commandery, and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，致仕，尋卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired; soon after he died and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired from office; he died soon afterward and was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 陳宗禮

translations.literal: Chen Zongli
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zongli

sentences.zh: 陳宗禮字立之。

translations.literal: Chen Zongli, style name Lizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zongli, whose style was Lizhi,

sentences.zh: 少貧力學，袁甫為江東提點刑獄，宗禮往問學焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and studied hard; Yuan Fu was judicial intendant of Jiangdong, and Zongli went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: was poor in youth but studied diligently. When Yuan Fu served as judicial intendant of Jiangdong, Zongli went to him to pursue his studies.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he was advanced as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of the Chunyou reign.

sentences.zh: 調邵武軍判官，入為國子正，遷太學博士、國子監丞，轉秘書省著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was assigned as signing clerk of Shaowu Army, entered the capital as director of the Imperial University, was promoted doctor of the Imperial Academy and vice director of the Directorate of Education, and transferred to assistant compiler in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as signing clerk of Shaowu Army, then entered the capital as director of the Imperial University; he was promoted to doctor of the Imperial Academy and vice director of the Directorate of Education, and transferred to assistant compiler in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入對，言火不循軌。

translations.literal: At audience he spoke of fire not following its orbit.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he spoke of a fire star wandering from its proper course.

sentences.zh: 帝以星變為憂，宗禮曰：「上天示戒，在陛下修德布政以回天意。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled by the change in the stars; Zongli said: 'Heaven shows a warning—the task lies with Your Majesty cultivating virtue and spreading good government to turn Heaven's will.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by the celestial omen. Zongli said, “Heaven is issuing a warning; Your Majesty must cultivate virtue and govern well to turn Heaven’s will.”

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天下方事於利欲之中，士大夫奔競趨利，惟至公可以遏之。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'All under Heaven is now immersed in profit and desire; scholar-officials rush and compete for gain—only supreme fairness can check this.'
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “The empire is now sunk in profit and desire; officials rush and scramble for gain. Only the utmost fairness can hold this in check.”

sentences.zh: 兼考功郎官，兼國史實錄院校勘，兼景獻府教授，升著作郎，遷尚左郎官兼右司。

translations.literal: He was concurrently director of the Merit Section, collator of the National History and Veritable Records Office, instructor at the Jingxian estate, promoted compiler, and transferred to left-section director concurrently right-section director.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as director of the Merit Section and collator of the National History and Veritable Records Office, and as instructor at the Jingxian estate; he was promoted to compiler and transferred to left-section director while also serving in the right section.

sentences.zh: 時丁大全擅國柄，以言為諱。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Daquan monopolized state power and made speech taboo.
