translations.idiomatic: At that time Ding Daquan monopolized state power and made frank speech taboo.

sentences.zh: 宗禮嘆曰：「此可一日居乎！」

translations.literal: Zongli sighed and said: 'Can one stay in this place even for a day!'
translations.idiomatic: Zongli sighed and said, “How can one remain in such a place even for a day!”

sentences.zh: 陛對，言：「願為宗社大計，毋但為倉廩府庫之小計；

translations.literal: At palace audience he said: 'I hope to plan for the altars of state and the ancestral temples, and not merely for the small calculations of granaries and treasuries;
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he said, “I pray Your Majesty will plan for the altars of state and the ancestral temples, and not merely for the petty accounts of granaries and treasuries;

sentences.zh: 願得天下四海之心，毋但得左右便嬖戚畹之心；

translations.literal: I hope to win the hearts of all under Heaven within the four seas, and not merely the hearts of those close at hand, favorites, and consort kin;
translations.idiomatic: I pray to win the hearts of all within the four seas, and not merely the hearts of those at Your Majesty’s side, of favorites, and of consort kin;

sentences.zh: 願寄腹心於忠良，毋但寄耳目於卑近；

translations.literal: I hope to entrust one's inmost heart to the loyal and good, and not merely one's eyes and ears to the base and near;
translations.idiomatic: I pray to entrust Your Majesty’s inmost trust to the loyal and good, and not merely Your Majesty’s eyes and ears to the base and near at hand;

sentences.zh: 願四通八達以來正人，毋但旁蹊曲徑類引貪濁。」

translations.literal: I hope to bring upright men by open roads in every direction, and not merely by side paths and crooked byways to bring in the greedy and corrupt.'
translations.idiomatic: I pray to bring upright men by open roads in every direction, and not by side paths and crooked byways to bring in the greedy and corrupt.”

sentences.zh: 拜太常少卿，以直寶謨閣、廣東提點刑獄進直煥章閣，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; as direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and judicial intendant of Guangdong he was advanced to direct academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, then transferred to director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; as direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and judicial intendant of Guangdong he was promoted to direct academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, then transferred to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史虞慮言追兩官，送永州居住。

translations.literal: Because Supervising Censor Yu Lü memorialized against him, two ranks were stripped and he was sent to live in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Supervising Censor Yu Lü impeached him, he was stripped of two ranks and sent to live in exile at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景定四年，拜侍御史，直龍圖閣、淮西轉運判官，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingding he was appointed palace censor, direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and transport vice commissioner of Huai West, and promoted minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jingding reign he was appointed palace censor, made direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and transport vice commissioner of Huai West, and promoted to minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人曹孝慶言罷。

translations.literal: Because Palace Diarist Cao Xiaoqing memorialized against him, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after Palace Diarist Cao Xiaoqing impeached him.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，兼侍講，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, he was given concurrent lecturer-in-waiting and appointed palace censor in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong ascended the throne, Zongli was given concurrent service as lecturer-in-waiting and appointed palace censor in attendance.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「恭儉之德自上躬始，清白之規自宮禁始，左右之言利者必斥，蹊隧之私獻者必誅。」

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'The virtue of reverence and frugality must begin with Your Majesty's own person; the rule of purity must begin within the palace precincts; those close at hand who speak of profit must be expelled, and those who make secret offerings by hidden paths must be punished.'
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said, “The virtue of reverence and frugality must begin with Your Majesty’s own person; the standard of purity must begin within the palace precincts; flatterers who speak of profit must be expelled, and those who make secret offerings by back channels must be punished.”

sentences.zh: 以《詩》進講，因奏：「帝王舉動，無微不顯，古人所以貴於慎獨也。」

translations.literal: Lecturing on the Book of Poetry, he memorialized: 'A ruler's every act, however slight, is never hidden—this is why the ancients prized careful solitude.'
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing on the Book of Poetry he memorialized, “A ruler’s every act, however slight, is never hidden from view—this is why the ancients prized vigilance in solitude.”

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was acting vice minister of Rites concurrently drafting censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of Rites while also serving as drafting censor.

sentences.zh: 進讀《孝宗聖訓》，因奏：「安危治亂，常起於一念慮之間，念慮少差，禍亂隨見。

translations.literal: Reading aloud Emperor Xiaozong's Sacred Instructions, he memorialized: 'Safety and danger, order and chaos, often arise in the space of a single thought; if thought strays even slightly, calamity and disorder follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: While reading aloud Emperor Xiaozong’s Sacred Instructions he memorialized, “Safety and danger, order and chaos, often arise in the space of a single thought; let thought stray even slightly and calamity follows at once.

sentences.zh: 天下之亂未有不起於微而成於著。」

translations.literal: There has never been disorder under Heaven that did not begin in what was slight and grow into what was manifest.'
translations.idiomatic: No disorder under Heaven has ever failed to begin in what was slight and grow into what was manifest.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「不以私意害公法，乃國家之福。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'Not letting private intent harm public law—this is the state's good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “When private intent does not harm public law, that is the state’s good fortune.”

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「孝宗家法，惟賞善罰惡為尤謹。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'In Xiaozong's family method, rewarding good and punishing evil was especially strict.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “In Xiaozong’s family method, rewarding good and punishing evil was especially strict.”

sentences.zh: 宗禮言：「有功不賞，有罪不罰，雖堯舜不能治天下，信不可不謹也。」

translations.literal: Zongli said: 'If merit is not rewarded and guilt is not punished, even Yao and Shun could not govern all under Heaven—this truly must be kept strict.'
translations.idiomatic: Zongli replied, “If merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, even Yao and Shun could not govern the empire. This truly cannot be treated lightly.”

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，尋權禮部尚書，乞奉祠，帝曰：「豈朕不足與有為耶？」

translations.literal: He was promoted vice minister of Rites, soon acting minister of Rites; he requested a sinecure post, and the Emperor said: 'Am I not worth achieving things with?'
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Rites and soon made acting minister of Rites; when he asked for a sinecure post, the emperor said, “Am I not worth accomplishing great things with?”

sentences.zh: 以華文閣直學士知隆興府，再辭，依舊職與待次差遣。

translations.literal: He was made direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and prefect of Longxing; he declined twice and was kept at his former rank with assignment awaiting turn.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and prefect of Longxing; he declined twice and was left at his former rank to await the next assignment.

sentences.zh: 逾年，依舊職廣東經略安撫使兼知廣州，加端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，尋兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: After a year, at his former rank he was made pacification commissioner of Guangdong concurrently prefect of Guangzhou, given academician of the Duanming Hall and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon acting vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made pacification commissioner of Guangdong and prefect of Guangzhou at his former rank, given the title academician of the Duanming Hall and made co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs; soon afterward he also served as acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「國所以立，曰天命人心。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'What a state stands upon is called the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said, “A state stands upon two things: the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 因其警而加敬畏，天命未有不可回也；

translations.literal: If because of its warnings one adds reverence and awe, the Mandate of Heaven has never been impossible to turn back;
translations.idiomatic: If, when Heaven sends warnings, one responds with reverence and awe, the Mandate of Heaven can still be turned back;

sentences.zh: 因其未墜而加綏定，人心未嘗不可回也。」

translations.literal: If before it has fallen one adds reassurance and stability, the hearts of the people have never been impossible to turn back.'
translations.idiomatic: and if, before the people’s hearts have fallen away, one adds reassurance and stability, those hearts can still be won back.”

sentences.zh: 卒官，遺表上，贈開府儀同三司、盱江郡侯，謚文定。

translations.literal: He died in office; his final memorial was submitted; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies and Marquis of Xujiang Commandery, with the posthumous title Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; when his final memorial was submitted, he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed posthumously as Marquis of Xujiang Commandery, with the posthumous title Wendi.

sentences.zh: 所著有《寄懷斐稿》、《曲轅散木集》、《兩朝奏議》、《經筵講義》、《經史明辯》、《經史管見》、《人物論》。

translations.literal: His writings include Drafts of Heartfelt Reflections, Collection of Crooked Axles and Scattered Wood, Memorials from Two Reigns, Lectures for the Classics Colloquium, Clarifications of Classics and History, My Humble Views on Classics and History, and Discourses on Personages.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Drafts of Heartfelt Reflections, Collection of Crooked Axles and Scattered Wood, Memorials from Two Reigns, Lectures for the Classics Colloquium, Clarifications of Classics and History, My Humble Views on Classics and History, and Discourses on Personages.

sentences.zh: 常楙字長孺，顯謨閣直學士同之曾孫。

translations.literal: Chang Mao, style name Changru, was the great-grandson of Xianmo Pavilion Direct Academician Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Mao, whose style was Changru, was the great-grandson of Xianmo Pavilion Direct Academician Chang Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 入太學。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 淳祐七年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunyou he was advanced as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of the Chunyou reign.

sentences.zh: 調常熟尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as assistant magistrate of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 公廉自持，不畏強禦，部使者交薦之。

translations.literal: Fair and incorrupt, he held himself strictly, did not fear the powerful, and circuit inspectors repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorruptible, he held himself to strict standards, did not fear the powerful, and circuit inspectors repeatedly recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 調婺州推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred as judicial assistant of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as judicial assistant of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 疏決滯訟，以剸繁裁劇稱。

translations.literal: He cleared and decided backlog lawsuits and was known for cutting through complexity and heavy cases.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the backlog of pending lawsuits and won renown for cutting through complex and difficult cases.

sentences.zh: 臨安府尹馬光祖又薦於朝，辟差平江府百萬倉檢察，不受和糴事例，戢吏卒苛取。

translations.literal: Lin'an Prefect Ma Guangzu again recommended him to court; he was invited to serve as inspector of the Million-Granary of Pingjiang Prefecture, refused commutation-purchase precedent fees, and restrained clerks and soldiers from harsh exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Prefect Ma Guangzu recommended him again to the court, and he was appointed inspector of the Million-Granary in Pingjiang Prefecture; he refused commutation-purchase precedent fees and restrained clerks and soldiers from harsh exactions.

sentences.zh: 發運使趙與芮兼提點刑獄，屬楙檢核，雪無錫翟氏冤獄。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhao Yurui, who also served as judicial intendant, assigned Mao to investigate and cleared the wrongful case of the Zhai clan of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Zhao Yurui, who also served as judicial intendant, assigned Mao to investigate and cleared the wrongful conviction of the Zhai clan of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 監江淮茶鹽所蕪湖局，不受商稅贏，光祖益敬之。

translations.literal: Supervising the Wuhu office of the Jianghuai Tea and Salt Agency, he would not accept excess commercial tax, and Guangzu respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the Wuhu office of the Jianghuai Tea and Salt Agency, he refused to accept excess commercial tax, and Guangzu respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 改知嘉定縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Jiading County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Jiading County.

sentences.zh: 歲大水，勸分和糴，按籍均敷。

translations.literal: In a year of great flood he urged sharing grain and commutation purchases and apportioned levies evenly according to the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe flooding he urged shared relief and commutation purchases, apportioning the burden evenly according to the household registers.

sentences.zh: 發運使王爚、提點刑獄孫子秀俱特薦於朝，簽書臨安府判官，不為權勢撓。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Wang Yao and Judicial Intendant Sun Zixiu both specially recommended him to court; as signing clerk of Lin'an Prefecture he was not swayed by power and influence.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Wang Yao and Judicial Intendant Sun Zixiu both specially recommended him to the court; as signing clerk of Lin'an Prefecture he would not yield to power and influence.

sentences.zh: 有為淮東提舉常平，辟楙提管，楙知其不可與共事，笑而卻之。

translations.literal: Someone served as Huaidong Commutation Intendant and invited Mao to manage affairs; Mao knew they could not work together and smilingly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When a man serving as Huaidong Commutation Intendant invited Mao to serve under him, Mao knew they could not work together and smilingly declined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，政府強楙行，遂拂衣去，朝野高之。

translations.literal: Before long the chief ministers forced Mao to go; he shook off his robes and left, and court and public held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the chief ministers forced him to accept; he shook off his robes and resigned, and both court and public held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 主管城南廂，聽訟嚴明，豪石益憚之。

translations.literal: In charge of the Chengnan ward, he heard cases with strict clarity, and powerful local families feared him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: While in charge of the Chengnan ward he heard cases with strict clarity, and the local magnates feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 都城火後，瓦礫充斥，差民船徙運，在籍者百五十家，惟二十有五家應役，余率為勢要宦官所庇。

translations.literal: After the capital fire, rubble filled the streets; civilian boats were conscripted for transport. Of one hundred fifty households on the register, only twenty-five answered corvée; the rest were mostly shielded by powerful men and eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fire, rubble filled the streets and civilian boats were conscripted for transport. Of the one hundred fifty households on the register, only twenty-five answered the corvée; the rest were mostly shielded by powerful men and eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 楙悉追之，不服者杖其人，械於他所，無不聽命。

translations.literal: Mao pursued them all; those who would not obey were beaten, shackled elsewhere, and none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Mao pursued them all; those who refused to obey were beaten and shackled elsewhere, and in the end none failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 又力拒戶部科買。

translations.literal: He also forcefully resisted the Ministry of Revenue's forced purchases.
translations.idiomatic: He also forcefully resisted the Ministry of Revenue’s forced purchases.

sentences.zh: 葉夢鼎、陳昉深期獎焉。

translations.literal: Ye Mengding and Chen Fang deeply praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengding and Chen Fang praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 添差臨安通判。

translations.literal: He was given an added appointment as vice prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was given an added appointment as vice prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 朝命鞫封樁庫吏範成獄，不肯承廟堂風旨，無辜者悉出之。

translations.literal: The court ordered him to try the case of sealed-reserve treasury clerk Fan Cheng; he would not follow the chief ministers' intended direction and released all who were innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered him to try the case of sealed-reserve treasury clerk Fan Cheng, he refused to follow the chief ministers’ intended direction and released all who were innocent.

sentences.zh: 知廣德軍。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 郡有水災，發社倉粟以活饑民，官吏難之，楙先發而後請專命之罪，置慈幼局，立先賢祠。

translations.literal: The commandery suffered flood; he opened communal granary grain to save starving people; officials objected, but Mao distributed first and afterward asked to be punished for acting without special authorization; he established a bureau for orphans and infants and built a shrine to former sages.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery suffered flooding, he opened the communal granary to save starving people; though officials objected, Mao distributed the grain first and afterward asked to be punished for acting without special authorization. He also established a bureau for orphans and infants and built a shrine to former sages.

sentences.zh: 故事，郡守秋苗例可得米千石，乃以代屬縣償大農綱欠。

translations.literal: By precedent a commandery prefect's autumn grain tax share could obtain one thousand shi of rice, which he used to substitute for subordinate counties' repayment of Grand Granary transport quota shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent a commandery prefect’s share of the autumn grain tax amounted to one thousand shi of rice; Mao used this to cover subordinate counties’ shortfalls in the Grand Granary transport quota.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，知無不言。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising censor and spoke frankly on everything he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed supervising censor, he spoke frankly on everything he knew.

sentences.zh: 嘗論天變及賈似道家爭田事，論繼皇子竑嗣，觸度宗怒，遷司農卿，尋為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He once memorialized on celestial changes and the land dispute of Jia Sidao's family, and argued for Prince Qi's succession; this provoked Duzong's anger, and he was transferred to minister of Agriculture, soon made transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized on celestial omens and the land dispute involving Jia Sidao’s family, and argued that Prince Qi should succeed to the throne; this provoked Duzong’s anger, and he was transferred to minister of Agriculture, then soon made transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 禁戢吏奸，不以急符督常賦。

translations.literal: He forbade and restrained clerical corruption and did not use urgent edicts to press regular tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade clerical corruption and did not use urgent edicts to press the collection of regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 海鹽歲為咸潮害稼，楙請於朝，捐金發粟，復輟己帑，大加修築新塘三千六百二十五丈，名曰海晏塘。

translations.literal: Each year in Haiyan saline tides harmed the crops; Mao requested funds and grain from court, also contributed from his own treasury, and greatly rebuilt a new embankment of three thousand six hundred twenty-five zhang, naming it the Haiyan Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in Haiyan saline tides damaged the crops; Mao petitioned the court for funds and grain, also contributed from his own treasury, and undertook a major reconstruction of a new embankment three thousand six hundred twenty-five zhang long, which he named the Haiyan Embankment.

sentences.zh: 是秋，風濤大作，塘不浸者尺許，民得奠居，歲復告稔，邑人德之。

translations.literal: That autumn wind and waves rose greatly; the embankment was submerged by only about one chi, the people were able to settle securely, the year again reported a good harvest, and the people of the district were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn wind and waves rose fiercely; the embankment was submerged by only about one chi, the people were able to live in safety, the year brought a good harvest again, and the people of the district were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 受四方民詞，務通下情。

translations.literal: Receiving petitions from the people in all directions, he strove to convey the feelings of those below.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving petitions from people throughout the empire, he strove to convey the concerns of those below to the court.

sentences.zh: 兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事，兼刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was concurrently rectifier of the various offices of the Secretariat-Chancellery and vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as rectifier of the various offices of the Secretariat-Chancellery and as vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 極論檢覆之弊。

translations.literal: He strongly argued against the abuses of review and reverification.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke forcefully against the abuses of the review-and-reverification system.

sentences.zh: 上進故事，首論雷雪非時之變，帝意不悅。

translations.literal: He submitted precedents to the throne, first discussing the untimely change of thunder and snow; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted precedents to the throne, opening with a discussion of untimely thunder and snow; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，不許，以集英殿修撰知平江。

translations.literal: He requested a sinecure post; this was not granted, and he was made compiler of the Jiying Hall and prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure post, but the request was denied; he was appointed compiler of the Jiying Hall and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 值旱。

translations.literal: A drought occurred.
translations.idiomatic: A drought struck the region.

sentences.zh: 故事，郡守合得緡錢十五萬，悉以為民食、軍餉助。

translations.literal: By precedent a commandery prefect was entitled to one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash, and he used all of it to aid the people's food and military rations.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent a prefect was entitled to one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash; Mao used all of it to aid the people’s food supply and military rations.

sentences.zh: 蠲苗九萬、稅十三萬、版帳十六萬，又蠲新苗二萬八千，大寬公私之力。

translations.literal: He remitted ninety thousand in seedling tax, one hundred thirty thousand in regular tax, and one hundred sixty thousand in ledger tax, and also remitted twenty-eight thousand in new seedling tax, greatly easing public and private burdens.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted ninety thousand in seedling tax, one hundred thirty thousand in regular tax, and one hundred sixty thousand in ledger tax, and also remitted twenty-eight thousand in new seedling tax, greatly easing the burden on both public and private purses.

sentences.zh: 飛蝗幾及境，疾風飄入太湖。

translations.literal: Flying locusts nearly reached the border; a fierce wind blew them into Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Flying locusts nearly reached the border, but a fierce wind blew them into Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 節浮費，修府庫。

translations.literal: He cut wasteful spending and repaired the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He cut wasteful spending and repaired the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 既代，有送還事例，自給吏卒外，余金萬楮，楙悉不受。

translations.literal: After his replacement, there were customary return fees; apart from provisions for clerks and soldiers, ten thousand in paper currency remained, and Mao refused it all.
translations.idiomatic: After he was replaced, customary return fees were offered; apart from provisions for his clerks and soldiers, ten thousand in paper currency remained, and Mao refused all of it.

sentences.zh: 吏驚曰：「人言常侍郎不愛錢，果然。」

translations.literal: A clerk exclaimed: 'People say Vice Minister Chang does not love money—it is truly so.'
translations.idiomatic: A clerk exclaimed, “People say Vice Minister Chang has no love of money—and it is true.”

sentences.zh: 改浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of Eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as pacification commissioner of Eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 值水災，捐萬楮以振之，復請糴於朝，得米萬石，蠲新苗三萬八千。

translations.literal: A flood disaster occurred; he donated ten thousand in paper currency for relief, again requested grain purchases from court, obtained ten thousand shi of rice, and remitted thirty-eight thousand in new seedling tax.
translations.idiomatic: When flooding struck, he donated ten thousand in paper currency for relief, petitioned the court for grain purchases, obtained ten thousand shi of rice, and remitted thirty-eight thousand in new seedling tax.

sentences.zh: 又以諸暨被水尤甚，給二萬楮付縣折運，民食不至乏絕。

translations.literal: Because Zhuji was especially flooded, he gave twenty thousand in paper currency to the county for transport conversion, and the people's food supply did not reach exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhuji was especially hard hit by the flood, he gave twenty thousand in paper currency to the county for transport and conversion, so that the people’s food supply did not run out.

sentences.zh: 民各祀於家。

translations.literal: The people each enshrined him in their homes.
translations.idiomatic: The people each enshrined him in their homes.

sentences.zh: 兩浙及會稽、山陰死者暴露與貧而無以為殮者，乃以十萬楮置普惠庫，取息造棺以給之。

translations.literal: For corpses left exposed in the Two Zhes and in Kuaiji and Shanyin, and for the poor who had no means of burial, he placed one hundred thousand in paper currency in the Universal Benefit Treasury, taking interest to make coffins and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: For corpses left exposed in the Two Zhes and in Kuaiji and Shanyin, and for the poor who had no means of burial, he placed one hundred thousand in paper currency in the Universal Benefit Treasury and used the interest to provide coffins.

sentences.zh: 尋以刑部侍郎召。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 申明期赦敘改法，與廟堂爭可否，辯偽關獄，救八倉虧欠免死罪，平反天井巷殺人獄，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: He clarified the law on scheduled amnesty reinstatement, debated with the chief ministers over approval and rejection, argued false customs-barrier cases, saved the eight granaries from capital-shortfall death penalties, reversed the Tianjing Lane murder case, and many lives were wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He clarified the law on scheduled amnesty reinstatement, debated its merits with the chief ministers, argued false customs-barrier cases, saved the eight granaries from death penalties for capital shortfalls, reversed the Tianjing Lane murder case, and preserved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中，封還隆國夫人從子黃進觀察使錄黃。

translations.literal: Concurrently drafting censor, he sealed and returned the recorded yellow appointing Lady Longguo's nephew Huang Jin as observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While also serving as drafting censor, he sealed and returned the recorded yellow appointing Huang Jin, nephew of Lady Longguo, as observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，似道以御書令委曲書行，楙迄不奉命。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; Sidao used an imperial letter ordering indirect writing to execute it, but Mao to the end would not obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; Sidao sent an imperial letter ordering that the appointment be executed by indirect drafting, but Mao never obeyed.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣待制提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was made expectant compiler of the Baozhang Pavilion and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed expectant compiler of the Baozhang Pavilion and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，拜吏部尚書，以老病辭，累詔不許，專官趣行甚峻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou he was appointed minister of Personnel; citing age and illness he declined; repeated edicts did not permit this; a special envoy was dispatched with stern urgent orders to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Deyou reign he was appointed minister of Personnel. He declined on grounds of age and illness, but repeated edicts refused to accept his resignation, and a special envoy was sent with stern orders that he proceed at once.

sentences.zh: 楙入見，首言「霅川之變，非其本心，置之死，過矣，不與立後，又過矣。

translations.literal: Mao entered audience and first spoke: 'The Zhechuan incident was not of his own heart's intent; to put him to death was excessive, and not to install an heir for him was excessive as well.
translations.idiomatic: Mao entered audience and began by saying, “The Zhechuan incident was not of Prince Qi's own heart's intent. To put him to death was excessive, and not to establish an heir for him was excessive as well.

sentences.zh: 巴陵帝王之胄，生不得正命，死不得血食，沉冤幽憤，郁結四五十年之久，不為妖為劄於冥冥中者幾希。

translations.literal: The Prince of Baling was of imperial lineage; in life he did not receive a proper fate, in death he receives no sacrificial offerings; deep wrong and hidden resentment, pent up for four or five decades — it would be rare indeed if he did not become a demon or bring calamity in the unseen realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Baling was of imperial blood. In life he was denied a proper fate; in death he receives no sacrificial offerings. Deep wrong and hidden resentment have been pent up for four or five decades — it would be rare indeed if he did not become a vengeful spirit or bring calamity from the unseen realm.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿搖浮議，特發神斷，宗社幸甚」。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not be swayed by loose talk but will issue a special divine decision — the altars of state would be greatly fortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will not be swayed by loose talk but will reach a resolute decision of your own — the altars of state would be greatly fortunate.”

sentences.zh: 於是詔國史院討論典故以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court ordered the Institute of National History to examine precedents and report.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court ordered the Institute of National History to examine historical precedents and report back.

sentences.zh: 明堂禮成，進端明殿學士、提領戶部財用，特與執政恩數。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall rites were completed, he was promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall and superintendent of Revenue finances, granted special treatment equal to a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall rites were completed, he was promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall and put in charge of Revenue finances, granted the special perquisites accorded a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 楙以國步方艱，非臣子貪榮之時，力辭恩數。

translations.literal: Mao, considering the state's step was perilous and that it was not a time for subjects to grasp at glory, forcefully declined the special treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Mao held that the dynasty was in grave peril and that this was no time for a subject to grasp at honors; he forcefully declined the special perquisites.

sentences.zh: 與廟堂議事不合，以疾謁告。

translations.literal: He disagreed with the chief ministers on policy and, citing illness, requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: He disagreed with the chief ministers on policy and, citing illness, requested leave of absence.

sentences.zh: 二年春，拜參知政事，為夏士林繳駁，拜疏出關，後六年卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was appointed vice grand councilor; Xia Shilin circulated a memorial of rejection; he submitted a memorial and left the capital; six years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was appointed vice grand councilor, but Xia Shilin circulated a memorial rejecting the appointment. Mao submitted a memorial and left the capital; six years later he died.

sentences.zh: 家鉉翁

translations.literal: Jia Xuanweng
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanweng

sentences.zh: 家鉉翁，眉州人。

translations.literal: Jia Xuanweng was a man of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanweng came from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補官。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he received an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He received an official appointment through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 累官知常州，政譽翕然。

translations.literal: Rising through offices he became prefect of Changzhou; his administrative reputation flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks, he became prefect of Changzhou, where his administrative reputation flourished.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提點刑獄，入為大理少卿，直華文閣，以秘閣修撰充紹興府長史，遷樞密都丞旨，知建寧府兼福建轉運副使，權戶部侍郎兼知臨安府、浙西安撫使，遷戶部侍郎，權侍右侍郎，仍兼樞密都丞旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Zhe judicial intendant, entered the capital as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, attached to Huawen Pavilion, served as Shaoxing prefect's chief administrator as Secretariat expectant compiler, promoted to Bureau of Military Affairs chief clerk, made prefect of Jianning concurrent Fujian transport vice commissioner, acting vice minister of Revenue concurrent prefect of Lin'an and Western Zhe pacification commissioner, promoted vice minister of Revenue, acting right vice minister, still concurrent Bureau chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial intendant of Eastern Zhe, then entered the capital as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was attached to Huawen Pavilion. As an expectant compiler of the Secretariat he served as chief administrator of Shaoxing Prefecture, was promoted to chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, appointed prefect of Jianning while also serving as Fujian transport vice commissioner, made acting vice minister of Revenue while also serving as prefect of Lin'an and Western Zhe pacification commissioner, promoted to vice minister of Revenue, made acting right vice minister while still retaining his post as Bureau chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 賜進士出身，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Granted jinshi status, he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and signing clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Granted jinshi status, he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and signing clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大元兵次近郊，丞相吳堅、賈餘慶檄告天下守令以城降，鉉翁獨不署。

translations.literal: When Great Yuan troops reached the suburbs, chancellors Wu Jian and Jia Yuqing issued proclamations ordering all prefects and magistrates to surrender their cities; Xuanweng alone did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan troops reached the suburbs of the capital, chancellors Wu Jian and Jia Yuqing issued proclamations ordering prefects and magistrates throughout the empire to surrender their cities. Xuanweng alone refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 元帥遣使至，欲加縛，鉉翁曰：「中書省無縛執政之理。」

translations.literal: The marshal sent envoys wishing to bind him; Xuanweng said: 'The Central Secretariat has no principle of binding a chief minister.'
translations.idiomatic: The marshal sent envoys intending to bind him. Xuanweng said, “The Central Secretariat has no precedent for binding a chief minister.”

sentences.zh: 堅奉表祈請於大元，以鉉翁介之，禮成不得命，留館中。

translations.literal: Jian submitted a petition praying to the Great Yuan, using Xuanweng as envoy; when the rites were complete he could not obtain permission to leave and was kept in the guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: Jian submitted a petition to the Yuan court with Xuanweng as envoy. When the rites were complete Xuanweng could not obtain permission to leave and was detained in the guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 聞宋亡，旦夕哭泣不食飲者數月。

translations.literal: Learning the Song had fallen, for months he wept day and night and would not eat or drink.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the Song had fallen, for months he wept day and night and would neither eat nor drink.

sentences.zh: 大元以其節高欲尊官之，以示南服。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan, because of his lofty integrity, wished to honor him with high office to display this to the southern domains.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court, impressed by his lofty integrity, wished to honor him with high office as a display to the southern domains.

sentences.zh: 鉉翁義不二君，辭無詭對。

translations.literal: Xuanweng's righteousness did not admit a second lord; he declined without crafty replies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanweng's loyalty would not admit a second sovereign; he declined without evasive or dissembling replies.

sentences.zh: 宋三宮北還，鉉翁再率故臣迎謁，伏地流涕，頓首謝奉使無狀，不能感動上衷，無以保存其國。

translations.literal: When the three Song palaces returned north, Xuanweng again led former officials to welcome and pay respects; he prostrated himself weeping, kowtowed and apologized that as envoy he had performed poorly, unable to move the emperor's heart, unable to preserve their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the three Song palaces were taken north, Xuanweng again led former officials to welcome and pay respects. He prostrated himself weeping, kowtowed, and apologized that as envoy he had performed so poorly that he could not move the emperor's heart and could not preserve the state.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不嘆息。

translations.literal: All who saw it sighed.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it sighed in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 文天祥女弟坐兄故，系奚官，鉉翁傾橐中裝贖出之，以歸其兄璧。

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang's younger sister, implicated because of her brother, was imprisoned as a palace servant; Xuanweng emptied his traveling funds to ransom her and returned her to her brother Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang's younger sister, implicated because of her brother, was imprisoned as a palace servant. Xuanweng emptied his traveling funds to ransom her and returned her to her brother Bi.

sentences.zh: 鉉翁狀貌奇偉，身長七尺，被服儼雅。

translations.literal: Xuanweng had a striking appearance, seven chi in height, dignified in dress.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanweng had a striking appearance, stood seven chi tall, and was dignified in dress and bearing.

sentences.zh: 其學邃於《春秋》，自號則堂，改館河間，乃以《春秋》教授弟子，數為諸生談宋故事及宋興亡之故，或流涕太息。

translations.literal: His learning was deep in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he styled himself Zetang; after changing residence to Hejian, he used the Spring and Autumn Annals to instruct disciples, often speaking to students of Song stories and the reasons for Song's rise and fall, sometimes weeping and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: His learning ran deep in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He styled himself Zetang. After taking up residence in Hejian, he used the Spring and Autumn Annals to instruct his disciples and often spoke to students of Song history and the causes of the dynasty's rise and fall, sometimes weeping and sighing as he did so.

sentences.zh: 大元成宗皇帝即位，放還，賜號「處士」，錫賫金幣，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzong of the Great Yuan took the throne, he was released, granted the title 'Recluse,' and bestowed gold and coins — all declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzong of the Yuan took the throne, Xuanweng was released and granted the title “Recluse,” along with gifts of gold and coin — all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 又數年以壽終。

translations.literal: Several years later he died at an advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 李庭芝

translations.literal: Li Tingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 李庭芝，字祥甫。

translations.literal: Li Tingzhi, style name Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi, whose style was Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 其先汴人，十二世同居，號「義門李氏」，後徙隨之應山縣。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Bian; twelve generations lived together and were called 'the Righteous Gate Li clan'; later they moved to Yingshan County in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were from Bian. Twelve generations of the family lived together and were known as “the Righteous Gate Li clan.” Later they moved to Yingshan County in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 金亡，襄、漢被兵，又徙隨。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, Xiang and Han were subject to military action, and they moved again to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin fell and Xiangyang and Hanzhong were ravaged by war, the family moved again to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 然特以武顯。

translations.literal: Yet they came to prominence specifically through martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the family came to prominence specifically through martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 庭芝生時，有芝產屋棟，鄉人聚觀，以為生男祥也，遂以名之。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi was born, fungus grew on the roof beams of the house; villagers gathered to look and took it as an auspicious sign of a male birth, and so named him accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi was born, fungus sprouted on the roof beams of the house. Villagers gathered to look and took it as an auspicious sign presaging the birth of a son, and so named him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 少穎異，日能誦數千言，而智識恒出長老之上。

translations.literal: From youth he was exceptionally bright; daily he could recite several thousand words, and his wisdom and insight always exceeded those of his elders.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was exceptionally bright. Each day he could recite several thousand words, and his wisdom and insight always surpassed those of his elders.

sentences.zh: 王旻守隨，庭芝年十八，告其諸父曰：「王公貪而不恤下，下多怨之，隨必亂，請徙家德安以避。」

translations.literal: When Wang Min defended Suizhou, Tingzhi at eighteen told his uncles: 'Lord Wang is greedy and does not care for those below; many below resent him; Suizhou will surely fall into disorder — please move the family to De'an to avoid it.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Min was defending Suizhou, the eighteen-year-old Tingzhi told his uncles, “Lord Wang is greedy and does not care for his men. Many below resent him. Suizhou will surely fall into disorder — please move our family to De'an to avoid it.”

sentences.zh: 諸父勉強從之，未浹旬，旻果為部曲挾之以叛，隨民死者甚眾。

translations.literal: His uncles reluctantly complied; within ten days Wang Min was indeed seized by his troops and forced into rebellion, and many people of Suizhou died.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles reluctantly complied. Within ten days Wang Min was indeed seized by his own troops and forced into rebellion, and a great many people of Suizhou died.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙末，江防甚急，庭芝得鄉舉不行，以策幹荊帥孟珙請自效。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiaxi reign, river defenses were urgent; Tingzhi received the local examination but did not proceed; he submitted a strategy to Jing commissioner Meng Gong and requested to offer himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiaxi reign, river defenses were urgently needed. Tingzhi passed the local examination but did not proceed to the capital; instead he submitted a strategy to the Jing commissioner Meng Gong and offered his services.

sentences.zh: 珙善相人，且夜夢車騎稱李尚書謁己，明日庭芝至。

translations.literal: Gong was skilled at physiognomy, and that night dreamed of chariots and horsemen announcing Vice Minister Li visiting him; the next day Tingzhi arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was skilled at reading faces, and that night he dreamed of chariots and horsemen announcing that Vice Minister Li was coming to visit him. The next day Tingzhi arrived.

sentences.zh: 珙見其魁偉，顧諸子曰：「吾相人多，無如李生者，其名位當過我。」

translations.literal: Gong saw his imposing stature and turned to his sons: 'I have read many faces, but none like this Li youth; his name and rank ought to surpass mine.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong saw his imposing stature and turned to his sons. “I have read many faces,” he said, “but none like this young Li. His name and rank will surpass mine.”

sentences.zh: 時四川有警，即以庭芝權施之建始縣。

translations.literal: At that time Sichuan had alarms, so Gong immediately made Tingzhi acting magistrate of Jianshi County in Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sichuan was under threat, so Gong immediately made Tingzhi acting magistrate of Jianshi County in Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庭芝至，訓農治兵，選壯士雜官軍教之。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi arrived, he trained farming and managed troops, selecting strong men to be mixed with regular troops for training.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi arrived, he organized farming and managed the troops, selecting strong men to train alongside the regular army.

sentences.zh: 期年，民皆知戰守，善馳逐，無事則植戈而耕，兵至則悉出而戰。

translations.literal: Within a year the people all knew warfare and defense, were skilled at pursuit; when at peace they planted spears and plowed; when troops came they all went out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the people all knew how to fight and defend, and were skilled at pursuit. In peacetime they planted spears and plowed the fields; when enemy troops came they all turned out to fight.

sentences.zh: 夔帥下其法於所部行之。

translations.literal: The Kui commander adopted his method and implemented it throughout his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Kui commander adopted his method and implemented it throughout his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 淳祐初始去，舉進士，中第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunyou he first left office, took the jinshi examination, and passed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunyou reign he left office, took the jinshi examination, and passed.

sentences.zh: 辟珙幕中，主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was invited into Gong's staff as superintendent of urgent paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: He was invited into Gong's staff as superintendent of urgent paperwork.

sentences.zh: 珙卒，遺表舉賈似道自代，而薦庭芝於似道，庭芝感珙知己，扶其柩葬之興國，即棄官歸，為珙行三年喪。

translations.literal: When Gong died, his final memorial recommended Jia Sidao to succeed himself and recommended Tingzhi to Sidao; Tingzhi, moved by Gong's recognition, escorted the coffin to bury him at Xingguo, immediately resigned office and returned, and observed three years' mourning for Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong died, his final memorial recommended Jia Sidao to succeed him and recommended Tingzhi to Sidao. Moved by Gong's recognition of his worth, Tingzhi escorted the coffin to bury him at Xingguo, immediately resigned his post, and observed three years of mourning for Gong.

sentences.zh: 似道鎮京湖，起為制置司參議，移鎮兩淮，與似道議柵清河五河口，增淮南烽百二十。

translations.literal: Sidao commanded Jing-Hu; he was summoned as planning commissioner of the military commission; transferred to command Liang-Huai; with Sidao he planned palisades at Qinghe's Five River Mouth and added one hundred twenty beacon towers on the Huai frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao took command of Jing-Hu, Tingzhi was summoned as planning commissioner of the military commission. When Sidao transferred to command the Two Huai, Tingzhi worked with him to plan palisades at the Five River Mouth of the Qinghe and added one hundred twenty beacon towers along the Huai frontier.

sentences.zh: 繼知濠州，復城荊山以備淮南。

translations.literal: Subsequently prefect of Haozhou; rebuilt Jingshan city to guard Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently made prefect of Haozhou and rebuilt Jingshan city to defend Huainan.

sentences.zh: 皆切中機會。

translations.literal: All were timely and grasped the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: All these measures were timely and seized the right opportunities.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，似道宣撫京湖，留庭芝權揚州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing, Sidao as pacification commissioner of Jing-Hu left Tingzhi acting at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Kaiqing reign, when Sidao went to Jing-Hu as pacification commissioner, he left Tingzhi as acting prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以大兵在蜀，奏知峽州，以防蜀江口。

translations.literal: Soon, with major troops in Shu, he memorialized to make him prefect of Xiasi to guard the Sichuan river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with major enemy forces in Shu, he memorialized to appoint Tingzhi prefect of Xiasi to guard the Sichuan river mouth.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以趙與芮為淮南制置，李應庚為參議官。

translations.literal: The court appointed Zhao Yourui as Huainan military commissioner, Li Yinggeng as planning officer.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhao Yourui as Huainan military commissioner and Li Yinggeng as planning officer.

sentences.zh: 應庚發兩路兵城南城，大暑中暍死者數萬。

translations.literal: Yinggeng mobilized troops from two routes south of the city wall; in great heat tens of thousands died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggeng mobilized troops from two routes south of the city wall. In the intense summer heat tens of thousands died of heatstroke.

sentences.zh: 李亶窺其無謀，奪漣水三城，渡淮奪南城。

translations.literal: Li Dan saw they had no strategy, seized three cities of Lianshui, crossed the Huai and seized the south city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dan saw that they had no strategy, seized three cities of Lianshui, crossed the Huai, and captured the south city.

sentences.zh: 鄂兵解，庭芝丁母憂去。

translations.literal: When the Ezhou relief ended, Tingzhi left for mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ezhou relief force was disbanded, Tingzhi left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 朝議擇守揚者，帝曰：「無如李庭芝。」

translations.literal: The court deliberated on who should guard Yangzhou; the emperor said: 'There is no one like Li Tingzhi.'
translations.idiomatic: When the court deliberated on who should defend Yangzhou, the emperor said, “There is no one like Li Tingzhi.”

sentences.zh: 乃奪情主管兩淮制置司事。

translations.literal: Thereupon, exempted from mourning, he was put in charge of the Huainan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, exempted from mourning, he was put in charge of the Two Huai military commission.

sentences.zh: 庭芝再破亶兵，殺亶將厲元帥，夷南城而歸。

translations.literal: Tingzhi twice defeated Dan's troops, killed Dan's general Li Yuanshuai, leveled the south city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi twice defeated Li Dan's troops, killed Dan's general Li Yuanshuai, razed the south city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 明年，復敗亶於喬村，破東海、石圃等城。

translations.literal: The next year he again defeated Dan at Qiaocun and captured Donghai, Shipu, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again defeated Li Dan at Qiaocun and captured Donghai, Shipu, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 又明年，亶降，徙三城民於通、泰之間。

translations.literal: The year after, Dan surrendered; the people of the three cities were relocated between Tong and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Li Dan surrendered, and the people of the three cities were relocated between Tongzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 又破蘄縣，殺守將。

translations.literal: He also captured Qixian and killed the defending general.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Qixian and killed the defending general.

sentences.zh: 庭芝初至揚時，揚新遭火，廬舍盡毀。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi first arrived at Yangzhou, Yang had recently suffered fire; dwellings were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi first arrived at Yangzhou, the city had recently suffered a fire and dwellings had been destroyed throughout.

sentences.zh: 州賴鹽為利，而亭戶多亡去，公私蕭然。

translations.literal: The prefecture depended on salt for profit, but salt workers had mostly fled; public and private were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture depended on salt for its revenue, but most of the salt workers had fled, and both public and private affairs were in ruin.

sentences.zh: 庭芝悉貸民負逋，假錢使為屋，屋成又免其假錢，凡一歲，官民居皆具。

translations.literal: Tingzhi fully remitted people's overdue debts, lent money for houses; when houses were built he remitted the loans too; within one year both official and private dwellings were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi fully remitted the people's overdue debts, lent them money to build houses, and when the houses were finished remitted those loans as well. Within a year both official and private dwellings were restored.

sentences.zh: 鑿河四十里入金沙餘慶場，以省車運。

translations.literal: He dug a canal forty li into the Jinsha Yuying salt field to save cart transport.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a canal forty li long to reach the Jinsha Yuying salt field, saving the cost of cart transport.

sentences.zh: 兼浚他運河，放亭戶負鹽二百餘萬。

translations.literal: He also dredged other transport canals and remitted over two million in salt workers' debts.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged other transport canals and remitted more than two million in salt workers' outstanding debts.

sentences.zh: 亭民無車運之勞，又得免所負，逃者皆來歸，鹽利大興。

translations.literal: Salt workers had no cart transport labor and also had debts remitted; fugitives all returned; salt profits greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The salt workers were spared the labor of cart transport and had their debts remitted as well. Fugitives all returned, and salt revenues greatly revived.

sentences.zh: 始，平山堂瞰揚城，大元兵至，則構望樓其上，張車弩以射城中。

translations.literal: Initially Ping Hill Hall overlooked Yang city; when Great Yuan troops came they built watch towers on it and deployed carriage crossbows to shoot into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ping Hill Hall overlooked Yangzhou. When Yuan troops arrived they built watchtowers on it and deployed carriage-mounted crossbows to shoot into the city.

sentences.zh: 庭芝乃築大城包之，城中募汴南流民二萬人以實之，有詔命為武銳軍。

translations.literal: Tingzhi then built a great wall enclosing it; recruited twenty thousand refugees from south of Bian in the city to fill it; an edict named them the Elite Militia Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi then built a great outer wall enclosing it. Within the city he recruited twenty thousand refugees from south of Bian to garrison it, and an edict named them the Elite Militia Army.

sentences.zh: 又大修學，為詩書、俎豆，與士行習射禮。

translations.literal: He also greatly repaired schools, made poetry books and sacrificial vessels, and practiced archery rites with scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He also greatly expanded the schools, provided books of poetry and sacrificial vessels, and practiced archery rites with the local scholars.

sentences.zh: 郡中有水旱，即命發廩，不足則以私財振之。

translations.literal: When the commandery had flood or drought, he immediately ordered granaries opened; when insufficient he used private wealth for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the commandery suffered flood or drought, he immediately ordered the granaries opened; when they were insufficient he used his private wealth for relief.

sentences.zh: 揚民德之如父母。

translations.literal: The people of Yang treated him as parents.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yangzhou regarded him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 劉槃自淮南入朝，帝問淮事，槃對曰：「李庭芝老成謹重，軍民安之。

translations.literal: Liu Pan entered court from Huainan; the emperor asked about Huai affairs; Pan replied: 'Li Tingzhi is seasoned and careful; soldiers and people are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pan came to court from Huainan, the emperor asked about affairs on the Huai frontier. Pan replied, “Li Tingzhi is seasoned and careful, and both soldiers and civilians are at peace under him.

sentences.zh: 今邊塵不驚，百度具舉，皆陛下委任得人之效也。」

translations.literal: Now the frontier is undisturbed, all affairs in order — all the effect of Your Majesty appointing the right men.'
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is now undisturbed and all affairs are in order — all the result of Your Majesty appointing the right men.”

sentences.zh: 咸淳五年，北兵圍襄陽急，夏貴入援，大敗虎尾州；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun, northern troops besieged Xiangyang urgently; Xia Gui entered to relieve and was heavily defeated at Huweizhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianchun reign, northern troops pressed the siege of Xiangyang. Xia Gui marched in to relieve the city and was heavily defeated at Huweizhou;

sentences.zh: 范文虎總諸兵再入，又敗，文虎以輕舠遁，兵亂，士卒溺漢水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Fan Wenhu commanded all troops to enter again, was defeated again; Wenhu fled in a light boat; the army fell into disorder; many soldiers drowned in the Hanshui and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhu then took overall command and marched in again, but was defeated once more. Wenhu fled in a light boat; the army fell into disorder, and a great many soldiers drowned in the Hanshui.

sentences.zh: 冬，命庭芝以京湖制置大使督師援襄陽。

translations.literal: In winter the court ordered Tingzhi as metropolitan commissioner of Jing-Hu to supervise troops to relieve Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court ordered Tingzhi, as metropolitan commissioner of Jing-Hu, to supervise the relief army for Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 文虎聞庭芝至，貽書似道曰：「吾將兵數萬入襄陽，一戰可平，但無使聽命於京閫，事成則功歸恩相矣。」

translations.literal: Wenhu heard Tingzhi had arrived and wrote to Sidao: 'I lead tens of thousands of troops into Xiangyang; one battle could pacify it — only do not let them take orders from the capital commander; when done the merit goes to Chancellor Sidao.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wenhu learned that Tingzhi had arrived, he wrote to Sidao: “I am leading tens of thousands of troops into Xiangyang. One battle could settle it — only do not let them take orders from the capital commander. When it is done, the credit will belong to Chancellor Sidao.”

sentences.zh: 似道喜，即除文虎福州觀察使，其兵從中制之。

translations.literal: Sidao was pleased and immediately made Wenhu observation commissioner of Fuzhou; his troops controlled matters from within.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was pleased and immediately made Wenhu observation commissioner of Fuzhou, allowing his troops to control operations from within.

sentences.zh: 文虎日攜美妾，走馬擊球軍中為樂。

translations.literal: Wenhu daily carried beautiful concubines, riding horses and playing polo in the army for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhu spent his days with beautiful concubines, riding horses and playing polo in camp for amusement.

sentences.zh: 庭芝屢欲進兵，曰：「吾取旨未至也。」

translations.literal: Tingzhi repeatedly wanted to advance troops and said: 'My imperial order has not yet arrived.'
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi repeatedly wanted to advance, but said, “My orders from the court have not yet arrived.”

sentences.zh: 明年六月，漢水溢，文虎不得已始一出師，未至鹿門，中道遁去。

translations.literal: The next year in the sixth month the Hanshui overflowed; Wenhu reluctantly finally marched once; before reaching Lumen he fled mid-route.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the sixth month, the Hanshui overflowed its banks. Wenhu reluctantly marched out at last, but before reaching Lumen he fled midway.

sentences.zh: 庭芝數自劾請代，不允，竟失襄陽。

translations.literal: Tingzhi repeatedly memorialized self-impeachment requesting replacement; not granted; ultimately Xiangyang was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi repeatedly memorialized impeaching himself and requesting replacement, but permission was not granted, and Xiangyang was ultimately lost.

sentences.zh: 陳宜中請誅文虎，似道庇之，止降一官知安慶府，而貶庭芝及部將蘇劉義、范友信廣南。

translations.literal: Chen Yizhong requested Wenhu's execution; Sidao sheltered him — only demoted one rank to prefect of Anqing; demoted Tingzhi and generals Su Liuyi and Fan Youxin to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong requested that Wenhu be executed, but Sidao sheltered him — Wenhu was merely demoted one rank and made prefect of Anqing, while Tingzhi and his generals Su Liuyi and Fan Youxin were banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 庭芝罷居京口。

translations.literal: Tingzhi dismissed lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed from office, Tingzhi lived at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元兵圍揚州，制置印應雷暴死，即起庭芝制置兩淮。

translations.literal: Before long Great Yuan troops besieged Yangzhou; commissioner Yin Yinglei died suddenly; Tingzhi was immediately recalled as commissioner of Liang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan troops besieged Yangzhou. The military commissioner Yin Yinglei died suddenly, and Tingzhi was immediately recalled to command the Two Huai.

sentences.zh: 庭芝請分淮西夏貴，而己得專力淮東，從之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi requested dividing Huainan west to Xia Gui while he himself could concentrate on Huaidong; granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi requested that western Huainan be assigned to Xia Gui while he concentrated on Huaidong, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十年，築清河口，詔以為清河軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he built Qinghekou; an edict made it Qinghe Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he fortified Qinghekou, and an edict established it as Qinghe Army.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大元兵破鄂，詔天下勤王，庭芝首遣兵為諸道倡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Great Yuan troops broke Ezhou; an edict called the empire to arms; Tingzhi first dispatched troops as leader of all routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yuan troops captured Ezhou. When an edict called the empire to arms, Tingzhi was the first to dispatch troops, leading all routes in the effort.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年春，似道兵潰蕪湖，沿江諸郡或降或遁，無一人能守者。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Deyou Sidao's army routed at Wuhu; along the river prefectures either surrendered or fled; not one could hold.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of the Deyou reign, Sidao's army was routed at Wuhu. Prefectures along the river either surrendered or fled — not one man could hold his post.

sentences.zh: 庭芝率所部郡縣城守。

translations.literal: Tingzhi led his command prefectures and counties in wall defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi led the prefectures and counties under his command in holding their walls.

sentences.zh: 有李虎者持招降榜入揚州，庭芝誅虎，焚其榜。

translations.literal: One Li Hu carried a surrender placard into Yangzhou; Tingzhi executed Hu and burned the placard.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Li Hu entered Yangzhou carrying a surrender placard. Tingzhi executed him and burned the placard.

sentences.zh: 總制張俊出戰，持孟之縉書來招降，庭芝焚書，梟俊五人於市。

translations.literal: Overall commander Zhang Jun went out to fight, brought Meng Zhijin's letter to sue for surrender; Tingzhi burned the letter and displayed five heads of Jun and others at market.
translations.idiomatic: The overall commander Zhang Jun went out to fight, bearing a letter from Meng Zhijin offering surrender. Tingzhi burned the letter and displayed the heads of Zhang Jun and four others in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 而日調苗再成戰其南，許文德戰其北，姜才、施忠戰其中。

translations.literal: Daily he deployed Miao Zaicheng to fight in the south, Xu Wende in the north, Jiang Cai and Shi Zhong in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he deployed Miao Zaicheng to fight in the south, Xu Wende in the north, and Jiang Cai and Shi Zhong in the center.

sentences.zh: 時出金帛牛酒燕犒將士，人人為之死鬥。

translations.literal: He frequently issued gold, silk, cattle, and wine in banquets to reward troops; each man fought to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently distributed gold, silk, cattle, and wine to feast and reward his troops, and every man fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦以督府金勞之，加庭芝參知政事。

translations.literal: The court also rewarded him with supervisory office gold and promoted Tingzhi to vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent gold from the supervisory office to reward him and promoted Tingzhi to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 七月，以知樞密院事征入朝，徙夏貴知揚州，貴不至，事遂已。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was summoned to court as Bureau of Military Affairs knowledge; Xia Gui was transferred to know Yangzhou; Gui did not arrive; the matter then ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was summoned to court as knowledge of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Xia Gui was transferred to take charge of Yangzhou, but Gui never arrived, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 十月，大元丞相伯顏入臨安，留元帥阿術軍鎮江以遏淮兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan entered Lin'an; left Marshal Azhu's army at Zhenjiang to block Huai troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Yuan chancellor Bayan entered Lin'an and left Marshal Azhu's army at Zhenjiang to block the Huai troops.

sentences.zh: 阿術攻揚久不拔，乃築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Azhu attacked Yang long unable to take it; then built a long encirclement to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu besieged Yangzhou for a long time without taking it, and then built a long encirclement to starve the city into submission.

sentences.zh: 冬，城中食盡，死者滿道。

translations.literal: In winter food in the city was exhausted and the dead filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the city ran out of food, and the dead filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，饑益甚，赴濠水死者日數百，道有死者，眾爭割啖之立盡。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month famine grew worse; those who went to the moat and died numbered hundreds each day; when there were dead on the road the crowd vied to cut and eat them until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: The following February the famine grew worse; hundreds each day threw themselves into the moat and drowned. When corpses lay in the streets, people fought to cut them up and eat them on the spot until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，謝太后及瀛國公為詔諭之降，庭芝登城曰：「奉詔守城，未聞有詔諭降也。」

translations.literal: When Song perished, Empress Dowager Xie and the Duke of Ying issued an edict instructing him to surrender; Tingzhi mounted the wall and said: 'I received an edict to hold the city; I have not heard an edict instructing surrender.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell, Empress Dowager Xie and the Duke of Ying issued an edict ordering him to surrender. Tingzhi mounted the wall and said, “I received an edict to hold this city; I have heard no edict ordering me to surrender.”

sentences.zh: 已而兩宮入朝，至瓜州，復詔庭芝曰：「比詔卿納款，日久未報，豈未悉吾意，尚欲固圉邪？

translations.literal: Before long the two palaces entered the court audience; reaching Guazhou they again instructed Tingzhi: 'Earlier we instructed you to submit; days pass without reply—do you not understand our intent and still wish to hold the walls?
translations.idiomatic: Soon the two palaces went north to court; reaching Guazhou they again instructed Tingzhi: “We earlier ordered you to submit, yet days pass without reply. Do you not understand our intent? Do you still mean to hold the walls?

sentences.zh: 今吾與嗣君既已臣伏，卿尚為誰守之？」

translations.literal: Now I and the heir have already submitted as subjects—for whom do you still hold it?'
translations.idiomatic: I and the heir have already submitted as subjects—for whom do you still hold the city?”

sentences.zh: 庭芝不答，命發弩射使者，斃一人，餘皆退去。

translations.literal: Tingzhi did not reply and ordered crossbows loosed at the envoys; one was killed and the rest all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi did not answer. He ordered crossbows fired at the envoys, killing one; the rest withdrew.

sentences.zh: 姜才出兵奪兩宮，不克，復閉城守。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai led troops out to seize the two palaces but did not succeed, and again closed the city to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai led troops out to recover the two palaces but failed, and the city was shut again for defense.

sentences.zh: 三月，夏貴以淮西降，阿術驅降兵至城下以示之，旌旗蔽野，幕客有以言覘庭芝者，庭芝曰：「吾惟一死而已。」

translations.literal: In the third month Xia Gui surrendered with Huai West; Azhu drove surrendered troops to the foot of the wall to display them, banners covering the wilds; a staff member spoke to probe Tingzhi, and Tingzhi said: 'I have only one death.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xia Gui surrendered with Huai West. Azhu drove surrendered troops to the foot of the wall to display them, banners covering the plain. A staff member tried to sound Tingzhi out; Tingzhi said, “I have only death left.”

sentences.zh: 阿術使者持詔來招降，庭芝開壁納使者，斬之，焚詔陴上。

translations.literal: Azhu’s envoy came bearing an edict to summon surrender; Tingzhi opened the rampart and admitted the envoy, beheaded him, and burned the edict on the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu’s envoy came with an edict summoning surrender. Tingzhi opened the gate, admitted the envoy, beheaded him, and burned the edict on the parapet.

sentences.zh: 已而知淮安州許文德、知盱眙軍張思聰、知泗州劉興祖皆以糧盡降。

translations.literal: Before long it was learned that Xu Wende, prefect of Huai’an, Zhang Sicong, military prefect of Xuyi, and Liu Xingzu, prefect of Sizhou, all surrendered when grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it was learned that Xu Wende of Huai’an, Zhang Sicong of Xuyi, and Liu Xingzu of Sizhou had all surrendered when their grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 庭芝猶括民間粟以給兵，粟盡，令官人出粟，粟又盡，令將校出粟，雜牛皮、曲糵以給之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi still levied grain from the populace to supply the troops; when grain was gone he ordered officials to contribute grain; when that too was gone he ordered officers to contribute grain, mixing ox hide and malt lees to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi still requisitioned grain from the people to feed the army. When that was gone he ordered officials to contribute grain; when that too was gone he ordered officers to contribute grain, mixing ox hide and malt lees to feed the men.

sentences.zh: 兵有烹子而食者，猶日出苦戰。

translations.literal: Among the troops were those who boiled their sons to eat, yet each day they still went out to fight bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers boiled their own sons for food, yet each day they still went out to fight desperately.

sentences.zh: 七月，阿術請赦庭芝焚詔之罪，使之降，有詔從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Azhu requested pardon for Tingzhi’s crime of burning the edict so that he might surrender; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Azhu asked that Tingzhi be pardoned for burning the edict so he might surrender; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 庭芝亦不納。

translations.literal: Tingzhi also did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi still would not accept.

sentences.zh: 是月，益王遣使以少保、左丞相召庭芝，庭芝以朱煥守揚，與姜才將兵七千人東入海，至泰州，阿術將兵追圍之。

translations.literal: That month the Prince of Yi sent envoys summoning Tingzhi as Junior Guardian and left grand councilor; Tingzhi left Zhu Huan to hold Yangzhou and with Jiang Cai led seven thousand troops eastward into the sea, reaching Taizhou; Azhu led troops in pursuit and encircled them.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Prince of Yi sent envoys summoning Tingzhi as Junior Guardian and left grand councilor. Tingzhi left Zhu Huan to hold Yangzhou and with Jiang Cai led seven thousand men east toward the sea, reaching Taizhou, where Azhu pursued and encircled them.

sentences.zh: 朱煥既以城降，驅庭芝將士妻子至泰州城下，陴將孫貴、胡惟孝等開門降。

translations.literal: Zhu Huan having surrendered the city, drove Tingzhi’s officers’, soldiers’, wives’, and children to the foot of Taizhou’s wall; rampart generals Sun Gui, Hu Weixiao, and others opened the gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan had already surrendered the city and drove the wives and children of Tingzhi’s officers and soldiers to the foot of Taizhou’s wall. Rampart generals Sun Gui, Hu Weixiao, and others opened the gate and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 庭芝聞變，赴蓮池，水淺不得死。

translations.literal: Tingzhi heard of the change, went to the lotus pond, but the water was shallow and he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the betrayal, Tingzhi threw himself into the lotus pond, but the water was too shallow and he could not drown.

sentences.zh: 被執至揚州，朱煥請曰：「揚自用兵以來，積骸滿野，皆庭芝與才所為，不殺之何俟？」

translations.literal: Seized and brought to Yangzhou, Zhu Huan requested: 'Since Yangzhou has been at war, piled bones fill the wilds—all done by Tingzhi and Cai; if we do not kill them, what are we waiting for?'
translations.idiomatic: Seized and brought back to Yangzhou, Zhu Huan pleaded: “Since the war began, bones have piled across the fields—all the work of Tingzhi and Cai. If we do not kill them now, when will we?”

sentences.zh: 於是斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 死之日，揚之民皆泣下。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the people of Yangzhou all wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died the people of Yangzhou wept.

sentences.zh: 有宋應龍者為泰州咨議官，泰守孫良臣之弟舜臣自軍中來說降，良臣召應龍與計，應龍極陳國家恩澤，君臣大義，請殺舜臣以戒持二心者，良臣不得已殺之。

translations.literal: There was Song Yinglong, Taizhou advisory official; Taizhou prefect Sun Liangchen’s younger brother Shunchen came from the army to urge surrender; Liangchen summoned Yinglong to deliberate; Yinglong fully stated the state’s grace and the great righteousness of ruler and minister, requesting Shunchen be killed to warn those of divided hearts; Liangchen had no choice but to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yinglong served as Taizhou advisory official. The prefect Sun Liangchen’s younger brother Shunchen came from the army to urge surrender. Liangchen summoned Yinglong to counsel him. Yinglong spoke at length of the state’s grace and the bond between ruler and minister, and asked that Shunchen be killed to warn those of divided loyalty; Liangchen reluctantly killed his brother.

sentences.zh: 及泰州降，應龍夫婦自經死。

translations.literal: When Taizhou surrendered, Yinglong and his wife hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizhou fell, Yinglong and his wife hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 提刑司諮議褚一正置司高郵，督戰被創，沒水死。

translations.literal: Judicial commission adviser Chu Yizheng established his office at Gaoyou, supervised battle, was wounded, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yizheng, adviser of the judicial commission, had established his office at Gaoyou; supervising the fighting he was wounded and drowned.

sentences.zh: 知興化縣胡拱辰，城破亦死。

translations.literal: Hu Gongchen, magistrate of Xinghua, also died when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gongchen, magistrate of Xinghua, also died when his city fell.

sentences.zh: 論曰：楊棟學本伊、洛，而尼於權臣，速謗召尤，誰之過歟？

translations.literal: The judgment says: Yang Dong’s learning traced to Yi and Luo, yet he was constrained by a powerful minister; swiftly slandered and inviting blame—whose fault was it?
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Yang Dong’s learning derived from the Yi and Luo masters, yet he was hemmed in by a powerful minister, quickly slandered and inviting blame—whose fault was that?

sentences.zh: 姚希得藹然君子。

translations.literal: Yao Xide was a gracious gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide was a gracious gentleman.

sentences.zh: 包恢以嚴為治，抑以衰世之民非可以縱馳待之耶？

translations.literal: Bao Hui governed with severity—yet is it not that the people of a declining age cannot be treated with loose reins?
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui governed with severity—yet can the people of a declining age really be handled with loose reins?

sentences.zh: 常挺、陳宗禮咸通濟，著聲望。

translations.literal: Chang Ting and Chen Zongli both were broadly accomplished and won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ting and Chen Zongli were both broadly accomplished and won lasting renown.

sentences.zh: 常楙晚訟皇子竑事，光明正大，公義炳然。

translations.literal: Chang Mao in his later years pleaded the case of Prince Qi—bright and upright, public righteousness shining clear.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Chang Mao pleaded the case of Prince Qi—open and upright, public justice shining clear.

sentences.zh: 家鉉翁義不二君，足為臣軌。

translations.literal: Jia Xuanweng’s righteousness allowed no second lord—enough to be a minister’s standard.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanweng’s loyalty to a single sovereign is enough to stand as a minister’s standard.

sentences.zh: 李庭芝死於國難，其可憫哉！

translations.literal: Li Tingzhi died in the nation’s calamity—how pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi died in the nation’s calamity—how pitiable!
